item.title: Game Pass Just Finally Got One of the Best Horror Games in Years
item.description: If you were to try to pick the best horror game of the 2020s so far, you’d have a very long list to choose from. Between multiple Resident Evil games, a successful revival of the Silent Hill franchise, and a slew of landmark indies like Signalis , the horror genre has been in a true renaissance over the past six years. The one game that sticks with me more than anything, though, is a three-hour psychological horror experience set on a stranded spaceship: developer Wrong Organ’s distressing Mouthwashing .

item.title: Careless dismissals give Australia route to series win
item.description: The winner of the third Test will finish the series top of the International Cricket Council's Test rankings [Getty Images] Third Test, Cape Town (day three of five) South Africa 329 & 140-4: Ackerman 62; Starc 2-29 Australia 429: Inglis 102; Harmer 4-104 South Africa lead by 40 runs Scorecard Batters carelessly gifting wickets to Australia... we have been here before. This time it was not England helping their opponents, although they will have taken note with a tour of South Africa to come this winter. South Africa's attempt to fight back in the decisive third Test against Australia was hurt by two poor strokes on day three. Having taken the last six Australian wickets for 99 runs in the morning despite Josh Inglis' second Test century, the Proteas began their second innings facing a deficit of exactly 100. They needed runs from their experienced opener and number three. Neither Aiden Markram nor David Bedingham could deliver. By the end, even captain Temba Bavuma had been tempted into a wild swipe to fall for 35. South Africa were 140-4, just 40 runs ahead, at the close. Australia are closing in. Weakness exposed by Australia In isolation, Markram's drive off Mitchell Starc straight into the hands of mid-off for one appeared the most egregious. The ball was the fullest of the six balls Markram faced but not there for him to play his trademark shot. Fielder Travis Head did not have to move. Worse, though, was the dismissal of Bedingham, who showed he had not learned from the first innings. Then, the right-hander top-edged a pull to Josh Hazlewood off the bowling of Starc. This time he repeated the shot, with Hazlewood the wicket-taking bowler. "That is just absolutely soft from David Bedingham," said former South Africa bowler Vernon Philander. "He knew they were going to target him in that zone. For the second time in the Test, he has fallen to the same ploy." The delivery which dismissed Markram was the fullest he had faced but still not full enough to be a driving length [CricViz] Given the prized position in South Africa's batting order on the back of strong domestic form for Durham in the County Championship and twin hundreds for Western Province in September, this score of 11 followed contributions of 49, 46 and 50 in his other four innings. He has got in but has not made a match-winning contribution. Batting in the key position of first drop, some would say that is more infuriating than not getting in at all. His dismissal, again like in the first innings, came shortly after being hit by a bouncer, with Starc clattering one into his chest on this occasion. When, after starting with two balls on a good length, Hazlewood went short again, Bedingham's eyes lit up. Ollie Robinson, Jofra Archer and co should have been taking note. It was the fifth time he has been dismissed pulling in his 18 Tests. On average he gets out playing that shot once every 13 deliveries. item.title: College football's traditions are for sale. Florida-Georgia shows the multi-million-dollar price tag
item.description: College football in the 2020s is a never-ending war between commerce and tradition, between a deep desire to preserve universities’ distinctive identities and an even deeper desire to make money off those distinctive identities. One of the war’s most notable battles is unfolding on the shores of the Atlantic Ocean in Jacksonville, Florida, where two of the SEC’s rivals meet every year in a celebrated, anticipated, cherished battle. (Well, not every year, but we’ll get to that.) Florida-Georgia — or Georgia-Florida, depending on whether you’re wearing red or blue to the game — is one of only three standing rivalry games played at a neutral site every year. (Texas-Oklahoma and Army-Navy are the others.) It’s achieved legendary status for both institutions; a pilgrimage to Jacksonville is a must for every Dawg and Gator. “It's one of the few events where twice as many people come to experience the game than actually go into the game,” says Michael Corrigan, president and CEO of Visit Jacksonville. “The stadium holds some 80,000 people. Well, there's 150,000 people that are tailgating or participating some way in that particular weekend. … It’s a three-and-a-half to four-hour commercial about Jacksonville, Florida on national TV.” “Jacksonville being a border town, there's just a lot of history and tradition,” Florida athletic director Scott Stricklin told Yahoo Sports. “It just holds a unique place in college football lore, and it's important for our school to maintain that part of the rivalry.” It’s a fantastic tradition, yes, but it’s also immensely lucrative, and as we’ve seen everywhere across the college football landscape, tradition doesn’t stand a chance against money. And what happens next in the Georgia-Florida-Jacksonville equation — which now includes Atlanta and Tampa for the next two years — could herald changes ahead for other major programs across the country. A general view of tailgating areas outside the stadium before the game between the Florida Gators and the Georgia Bulldogs on November 1, 2025 at EverBank Field in Jacksonville. Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The World’s Largest Outdoor Branding Opportunity Corporate and brand-minded interests have dubbed this year’s Florida-Georgia game the “Invesco QQQ Atlanta Gridiron Classic,” but everyone involved knows it by its traditional name: the World’s Largest Outdoor Cocktail Party. When you’re a student, you hang wherever you can find a beer and a bed; Frat Beach in nearby St. Simons Island is a longstanding Georgia tradition. When you’re an alum with a bit more disposable income, you rent a Duval County Airbnb and whip up themed cocktails. And everyone, young and old, descends on Jacksonville’s EverBank Stadium, dividing neatly into “Georgia” and “Florida” quadrants. Well, except this year and next. Because EverBank is undergoing massive renovations, the party has moved to Atlanta this weekend and Tampa next year. The game will again take place in NFL stadiums — Mercedes-Benz in

item.title: Ondo approves state burial for Fasoranti
item.description: By Dayo Johnson, Akure Ondo State Governor, Lucky Aiyedatiwa, has set up a committee to organise a state burial for the late Afenifere leader, Pa Reuben Famuyide Fasoranti, who died at the age of 100. According to a statement issued in Akure by the governor’s Chief Press Secretary, Prince Ebenezer Adeniyan, the committee will work with the Fasoranti family and the leadership of Afenifere to organise a befitting burial for the elder statesman. The committee is chaired by the state Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice, Dr Kayode Ajulo, SAN, while Apostle Eniola Olushola will serve as secretary. Other members are Hon. Gbenga Fasua, Mr Gbenga Atiba, Mrs Kosemani Kolawole, Rt. Hon. Bakkita Bello, Hon. Idowu Otetubi, Erelu Modupe Martins, Mr George Asonja, Esq., Mr Muyiwa Ogunyemi, Hon. Stephen Abitogun and Mr Adetunji Gbenga. Adeniyan said the state government decided to honour Fasoranti with a state burial in recognition of his contributions to Ondo State, Yorubaland and Nigeria. He said Aiyedatiwa believed the late Afenifere leader deserved to be celebrated for his life of service, wisdom and selfless leadership. The governor also reaffirmed the government’s commitment to ensuring that the burial reflects Fasoranti’s contributions to society. The committee is expected to coordinate the arrangements in consultation with the family and Afenifere leadership to ensure a dignified farewell for the late nationalist. The post Ondo approves state burial for Fasoranti appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Ronaldo thanks fans after winning greatest Ballon d’Or award
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Cristiano Ronaldo has appreciated his fans and supporters around the world after his 2008 Ballon d’Or-winning season was voted the best in the history of the prestigious individual football award in a public poll organised to celebrate its 70th anniversary. The Ballon d’Or announced Ronaldo as the winner of its “Ballon d’Or of All Time” (BOAT) vote on Wednesday, after fans had their say in a poll that made them choose their favourite Ballon d’Or-winning season. In a post on X today, Ronaldo appreciated his fans, as he dedicated the award to them. He wrote: “Football belongs to the fans! Thank you to all the fans around the world, the Ballon D’Or of All Time is also yours.” Football belongs to the fans! Thank you to all the fans around the world, the Ballon D’Or of All Time is also yours. pic.twitter.com/S0sLDNiUUY — Cristiano Ronaldo (@Cristiano) October 29, 2026 Ronaldo’s message followed his victory in the inaugural Ballon d’Or of All Time (BOAT) public vote, organised by France Football. Fans chose their favourite Ballon d’Or-winning season, and Ronaldo’s 2008 campaign finished ahead of Lionel Messi’s 2012 season. The 41-year-old winning season came with Manchester United in 2007–08, where he scored 42 goals in all competitions, including 31 in the Premier League and seven in the Champions League. United won both the Premier League and Champions League, with Ronaldo scoring in the final against Chelsea. His league tally earned him the European Golden Shoe, and he went on to win his first Ballon d’Or later that year. The Portuguese legend subsequently won the award four more times, in 2013, 2014, 2016 and 2017, taking his career tally to five. Lionel Messi’s 2012 season finished second in the poll, with Ronaldo’s 2017 campaign third. Messi’s 2023 season took fourth, while Ronaldo’s 2016 campaign rounded out the top five. The top ten also includes Ronaldo’s 2014 and 2013 seasons, plus Messi’s 2015, 2011 and 2009 campaigns. The BOAT vote was a fan poll celebrating the award’s 70th anniversary, rather than a new Ballon d’Or trophy. Voting opened on October 1 and closed on October 27, with the result announced on October 28. The post Ronaldo thanks fans after winning greatest Ballon d’Or award appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 'Celeste' and 'Towerfall' Delisted From Xbox as Dev Joins Boycott
item.description: Celeste and Towerfall are no longer on Xbox. Developer Maddy Thorson has explained why in a social media post: to support the ongoing pro-Palestinian Boycott, Divestment, and Sanctions (BDS) movement against Microsoft. Thorson, who led development of both titles at Maddy Makes Games, confirmed in a post on Bluesky that her studio delisted both games from the platform.

item.title: Cowboys RB Javonte Williams considered retirement before signing with team
item.description: Dallas Cowboys running back Javonte Williams has revealed that he nearly walked away from the NFL before finding a new lease on his football career in Dallas. The 26-year-old admitted that his time with the Denver Broncos left him questioning his future in the sport before joining the Cowboys and rediscovering his passion for the game. Speaking on Down 2 Business on Wednesday, Williams opened up about how close he came to retiring and explained how his move to Dallas completely changed his outlook. Dallas Cowboys RB Javonte Williams said on @downs2business that following his time with the Denver Broncos and before signing with the Cowboys he gave thought to retiring, just with everything that had happened in his career at that point. "I was really about to just hang up the cleats." "No disrespect to nobody in Denver or nothing like that, I respect everybody over there, I respect what they got going on… just coming to Dallas it felt like it’s a new awakening. I felt like a rebirth." "Just leaving there and coming here, the coaches believing in me, everybody just like lifting me up. It kind of felt like UNC all over again. Me just going out there just playing, having fun." "I just fell in love with the game again. I really had lost love for the game… I had already bought a crib… I’m like I might just start my real estate or something." Javonte gave credit to his faith and family for helping him give things another go. — RJ Ochoa (@rjochoa) October 28, 2026 “I was really about to just hang up the cleats,” Williams said. “No disrespect to anybody in Denver… just coming to Dallas it felt like it’s a new awakening.” Williams also revealed that he had “lost love for the game” and had apparently considered pursuing a career in real estate instead. MORE: Bengals have finally fixed issue that’s plagued them since 2021-22 Super Bowl run Williams finds new life after difficult Broncos tenure Oct 26, 2026; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Dallas Cowboys running back Javonte Williams (33) celebrates his touchdown run against the Philadelphia Eagles during the fourth quarter at Lincoln Financial Field. Mandatory Credit: Eric Hartline-Imagn Images Williams spent his first four NFL seasons with Denver after the Broncos selected him in the second round of the NFL Draft. He enjoyed a promising rookie campaign in 2022, but injuries and inconsistent performances hampered his progress over the following three seasons. By the time his tenure in Denver ended, Williams was facing uncertainty about his future in football. His eventual move to Dallas, however, proved to be a turning point. The Cowboys signed Williams for the 2025 season, giving the running back an opportunity to rebuild his career. He responded with the best statistical season of his NFL career, rushing for 1,201 yards and 11 touchdowns. His impressive performances convinced Dallas to sign him to a three-year, $24 million contract this offseason, securing his future with the franchise. MORE: Colts player a

item.title: Fantasy Football Trade Advice: Tony Pollard is a Sell-High Running Back
item.description: Oct 25, 2026; Nashville, Tennessee, USA; Tennessee Titans running back Tony Pollard (20) cuts back against the Cleveland Browns during the second half at Nissan Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Steve Roberts-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Fantasy football trade season is underway. Most leagues are about 50% deep into their regular season. Many fantasy managers are in the playoff chase, and a team resurgence is needed. Completing a profitable trade might be just what the doctor ordered. Today, I make the case for selling one man at a high price - Tony Pollard. Tony Pollard's Fantasy Breakout Pollard's Week 7 provides an opportunity to create a strong trade proposal. He ran for season-highs in attempts (25), yards (129), and touchdowns (3). Much of that came thanks to his depth chart; Tyjae Spears was inactive. In fact, Pollard set season highs in consecutive games. The Titans ball-carrier ran the ball 19 times for 76 yards in Week 6, which was his best of 2026 at the time. The Titans might have found something offensively over their last two games. They have scored 50 points over those games against the Browns and Colts. Before that, the Titans had scored only 20 points in one game. I'm not yet sold on the Titans offense. They have one win and six losses. The team ranks 31st in EPA per Play on offense . ESPN's FPI lists the Titans as the 2nd-worst offense in the NFL, ahead of the Eagles. Pollard's median fantasy points scored this season in standard-scoring formats is 7.6. That earns him must-sit status in fantasy football on a weekly basis. The passing game is Pollard's biggest knock. He averages 1.6 receptions per game, and three of those came in Week 7 without Spears. The Titans cannot be trusted to support a running back. Not only are they a bad football team, but they are projected to often be in game scripts that work against Pollard. Going back to ESPN's FPI, the Titans are rated the 2nd-worst team in the NFL overall. In that metric, the Titans rate at minus-6.3, as of October 29. In other words, in a neutral environment, the Titans are expected to lose to the average NFL team by 6.3 points. Those teams would exemplify that, such as the Steelers and Packers. The Titans are FPI-rated 12.2 points worse than the 49ers, the best team on paper. The Titans shall often end up in pass scripts when trailing. That means less running and more passing. Once Spears returns, Pollard's volume will be largely capped at the ground game. He has ranged around a 50% snap rate with Spears active and a median of 14 rushing attempts. Tony Pollard Trade Rumors Less than two weeks to the trade deadline, Pollard is hot on the trade block . Conversations suggest multiple teams have interest. But two of the most prominent teams right now are the New York Giants and Seattle Seahawks. As a Pollard owner, I would not love those landing spots. item.title: Anthony Joshua coach reacts to Tyson Fury’s ‘traitor’ jibe based on shared history
item.description: Ben Davison has played down Tyson Fury ’s “tongue-in-cheek” claim that the coach is a “traitor”, after Davison reunited with Anthony Joshua ahead of a fight with the “Gypsy King”. Davison coached Fury in 2018, when the heavyweight returned to boxing after a two-year hiatus, guiding his fellow Briton to wins over Francesco Pianeta and Sefer Seferi before a draw with Deontay Wilder – in a fight that most fans felt Fury had won. Fury remained with Davison for victories over Tom Schwarz and Otto Wallin, but he split from the coach ahead of a 2020 rematch with Wilder, which Fury won via stoppage – before repeating that result in 2021. Tyson Fury (left) and his former trainer Ben Davison before their split (PA) Davison then partnered with Joshua in 2023, leading “AJ” to knockouts of Wallin and Francis Ngannou, but the pair parted ways after a stoppage loss to Daniel Dubois in 2024. Joshua has fought twice since, stopping YouTuber Jake Paul in December and Kristian Prenga in July, and now he has reunited with Davison ahead of a long-awaited super-fight with Fury . Fury vs Joshua will take place on 11 December, as the former world heavyweight champions headline at Cardiff’s Principality Stadium, and backstage at a press conference to promote that bout, Fury playfully labelled Davison a “traitor”. “I think it’s tongue in cheek,” Davison told Playbook Boxing , powered by Betway . “I’ll be honest, I don’t think he cares who works with AJ. But I think most importantly, I spent a lot of time with him, and I think deep down he knows what type of person I am. “I think he would say: ‘I know Ben’s a good guy.’ He’s smart enough to understand that boxing is a business, and hopefully he feels the same way I do, where it doesn’t have an impact. Like I say, he could say whatever it is that he wanted to – call me this, call me that, whatever; it wouldn’t change how things are, because deep down I have the same, where I know he’s a good guy. “Of course it’s a little bit awkward, [but] I’ve got a lot of love and a lot of respect for Tyson [...] It’s solely business. He can say whatever he wanted to say. He could call me ‘rotten’ if he wanted to. Davison checking on Anthony Joshua after the latter’s KO by Daniel Dubois (Getty) “I never fell out with any ex-fighters that I’ve worked with, and it’s important to me that stays the same. But at the same time, I’ve got a fantastic relationship and a lot of love for AJ as well.” As Davison, 33, prepares to coach Joshua against Fury, the trainer has actually played down the significance of his past with the Gypsy King. Saying there is “not really” a conflict of interest, Davison explained: “I think Tyson’s developed as a fighter. There’s nothing that I would know about him that you couldn’t see by watching one of his fights, in terms of boxing. “Outside of that, I think that’s something that AJ respects: I never go to AJ and talk to him about Tyson. I think that’s something that he can see; there’s a level of integrity there.” F

item.title: Maryland offers buy-one, get-two-free tickets ahead of Illinois matchup
item.description: Sep 26, 2026; College Park, Maryland, USA; The Maryland Terrapins warm up before a game against the UCLA Bruins at SECU Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jamie Sabau-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Maryland is pulling out all the stops to pack SECU Stadium ahead of Saturday’s matchup against Illinois, including a ticket promotion that gives fans two free tickets with the purchase of one. The Terrapins announced the Halloween promotion Monday, giving fans the unique opportunity to buy three tickets for the price of one. Thus, the orange and blue may have a tougher task in College Park than they originally planned. The unusual promotion comes amid a disastrous season for Maryland, which sits at 2-5 overall and 0-4 in Big Ten play. The Terrapins recently fired head coach Mike Locksley following their 12th consecutive conference loss. Maryland is also offering students the chance to win free tuition for the spring semester if they attend Saturday’s game and remain through the fourth quarter. Maryland only averaged just over 40,000 fans in 2025, ranking near the bottom of the Big Ten in attendance. With interim head coach Aazaar Abdul-Rahim making his debut, Maryland is hoping discounted tickets and a tuition giveaway will help create a home-field advantage against the Illini.

This weekend could go a long way toward answering doubters and putting the Hoosiers back in the driver’s seat for a repeat conference title. item.title: Playoff primer | Sturgis-area football squads open the post season
item.description: When the MHSAA football playoffs start this weekend, five of our local teams will begin their quests. For 8-player football, three squads in Colon, Marcellus and Mendon have aspirations of traveling the better than seven-hour trip north. The Superior Dome on the campus of Northern Michigan University will once again host the 8-player football finals. For 11-player, both Bronson and Constantine have qualified for the playoffs. They also have aspirations of making it to the MHSAA football finals, which are played once again at Ford Field in Detroit. Here's a look at each team's matchup this weekend. CROSS COUNTRY CROWNS: Sturgis girls, Centreville boys claim St. Joe County team titles VOTE VOTE VOTE: Cast your votes for the Footballer of the Week, presented by Glen Oaks CC! Bridgman at Colon, Friday at 7 p.m. Both Bridgman and Colon finished the season with identical 8-1 records. Colon, by virtue of more playoff points, earned the home game. Head coach Robbie Hattan and the Magi wanted to play the contest on Friday night and earned that ability by having a successful regular season. The Bees come in swarming opponents with an average of nearly 50 points per game. They also picked up a forfeit win over Wyoming Tri-Unity Christian late in the season, but Bridgman has been able to move the football on everyone this year. The lone loss came back in the middle of the year, 56-28, to Grand Rapids Sacred Heart. Hattan said the Bees are a well-coached team and his program understands that. Avoiding miscues is a big part of Bridgman's success this year. Being physical has been as well. Colon knows Friday's game will probably be nothing different. "We need to establish our run game. Bridgman is very physical and we have to match their physicality," Hattan said. "Hopefully this place is rocking and we make our community proud." Colon is no slouch offensively, either. The Magi put up 39 per contest and only two opponents — Climax-Scotts and Mendon, a pair of playoff teams — kept them under 40. Hattan, in his return to lead the Magi, has been more than happy with his team's performance this year. The program is looking forward to another playoff appearance. "It's a great feeling — going into the season, we set some high goals," he said. "It's great to see the hard work that the kids have put in pay off." The winner of Friday's game will take on the winner of Climax-Scotts and Concord. Marcellus at Litchfield, Friday at 7 p.m. Marcellus had a successful regular season, winning six of their games. The Wildcats had three separate two-game win streaks during the year, but dropped their regular-season finale to Fennville in a 42-22 decision. But head coach Nate Davies and the Cats have a lot of confidence in themselves. A big win earlier this year over Grand Rapids Sacred Heart (34-26) helped instill that. And even in a 56-52 defeat against Climax-Scotts, the Cats showed they could score points against solid opponents. Now, they hit the road on Friday to play at Lit

item.title: As Houston Astros look to fill needs, here are MLB's 20 best free agents this offseason
item.description: Tarik Skubal (left), Jazz Chisholm (center) and Randy Arozarena (right) are some of the top free agents in baseball for the 2026-27 offseason. (Getty Images) The Milwaukee Brewers capped off a dominant season in fitting fashion, capturing the franchise's first World Series on Wednesday after winning 103 games in the regular season, then going 11-2 in the postseason. Now, the rest of baseball will try to catch them. Baseball free agency has started with players able to sign with new teams as soon as 4 p.m. Monday. It could be a tight window, because Major League Baseball's collective bargaining agreement expires at midnight on Dec. 1 , which could lead to a long lockout. However, when this happened in 2021, there was a flurry of free agent activity before the CBA expired, including the Texas Rangers signing both Corey Seager and Marcus Semien to huge deals. The Astros, who have a few key players of their own hitting free agency , have holes to fill, particularly in the outfield and starting rotation. Here's how we rank the 20 best free agents to hit the open market this offseason… 1. Tarik Skubal, starting pitcher, Dodgers Tarik Skubal of the Los Angeles Dodgers looks on from the dugout prior to Game Four of the National League Championship Series between the Milwaukee Brewers and the Los Angeles Dodgers at UNIQLO Field at Dodger Stadium on Thursday, October 15, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Daniel Shirey/MLB Photos via Getty Images) It can't even be debated who the top prize on the free agent market is this offseason. The only question is just how much money is he going to get. The two-time Cy Young Award winner turns 30 in November, meaning whoever signs him is getting an ace in his prime. If the Phillies gave Zack Wheeler $42 million per year and the Tigers gave Framber Valdez $38.3 million per year , then Skubal's got to get at least $50 million a year, right? 2. Freddy Peralta, starting pitcher, Rays Freddy Peralta of the Tampa Bay Rays walks back to the dugout after pitching in the first inning during Game Three of the 2026 World Series presented by Capital One between the Milwaukee Brewers and the Tampa Bay Rays at Tropicana Field on Monday, October 26, 2026 in St. Petersburg, Florida. (Mary DeCicco/MLB Photos via Getty Images) The 30-year-old Peralta will be an interesting case to watch, because he was one of the best pitchers in baseball in 2025 when he finished fifth in the National League Cy Young Award race with the Milwaukee Brewers, but then got traded to the New York Mets where he struggled for the first half of 2026. The Mets traded him to the Rays and Peralta suddenly found his way, including being named MVP of the American League Championship Series. 3. Teruaki Sato, third baseman, Japan Teruaki Sato of Team Japan hits an RBI double in the eighth inning during the 2026 World Baseball Classic Pool C game between Australia and Japan at Tokyo Dome on March 8, 2026 in Tokyo, Japan. (Toru Hanai/Getty Images) The best offensive pla

item.title: Arsenal could be set for major injury boosts ahead of Liverpool clash
item.description: Arsenal could be set for major injury boosts ahead of Liverpool clash Arsenal Injury Update Before Liverpool: Rice, Madueke and Saliba Latest Ahead of Anfield Arsenal go to Anfield with little room for self-inflicted problems. The defeat to Fleetwood in the Carabao Cup was bad enough on its own, but the bigger issue for Mikel Arteta is what it may have done to his squad depth before a major league test against Liverpool. The immediate concern is Max Dowman. He was sent off against Fleetwood, leaving Arsenal short in the wide areas at exactly the wrong moment. The club plan to appeal the straight red and hope the three-match ban is overturned in time for Sunday, but that now sits with the FA. Until there is a verdict, it remains an avoidable distraction. Declan Rice and Noni Madueke in frame There is better news elsewhere. Noni Madueke missed the Fleetwood game because of an ankle issue, but the expectation is that the injury is not serious. Arsenal are optimistic he will be available to start on the right at Anfield, which matters given the current lack of options. Declan Rice is in a similar category. He was left out entirely in midweek after feeling hamstring tightness in the second half of the win over Everton. Arsenal have handled him carefully all season and already pulled him from England duty during the last international break to manage his workload. That caution has not changed, but a full week without a midweek fixture gives him a proper chance of being ready for Liverpool. Photo IMAGO Christos Tzolis nearing return Christos Tzolis is also moving closer. He has been sidelined for nearly a month after suffering a hamstring injury on Greece duty, but his recovery has gone well. Fleetwood came too early for him, though there is a realistic possibility he makes the squad this weekend if first-team training goes smoothly over the next few days. William Saliba recovery offers Arsenal lift The longer-term update concerns William Saliba, and this is arguably the most significant one. He has not featured at all this season after Arsenal decided in the summer that a long-term back problem required a proper lay-off rather than a patch-up job. That was the sensible call. Saliba has spent the last three weeks back on the grass doing individual work and is edging towards a return to full training. If that next step passes without any setback, he could be back in an Arsenal matchday squad before the international break. So this is where Arsenal stand. Rice and Madueke are expected to have a chance, Tzolis is close, Dowman waits on an appeal, and Saliba is finally moving in the right direction. Ahead of Anfield, that counts as progress.

item.title: Rio Ngumoha heaps praise on Liverpool teammate after Chelsea win
item.description: Rio Ngumoha heaps praise on Liverpool teammate after Chelsea win Rio Ngumoha and Trey Nyoni show why Liverpool’s future is already arriving Liverpool’s young players took centre stage against Chelsea, and the headline was familiar. Rio Ngumoha looked sharp, direct and confident against his former club, again showing why he is viewed as one of the brightest prospects at Anfield. He drifted out of the contest in the second half, that much is true, but the damage had already been done in terms of impression. For long spells, he looked like the most dangerous attacking player on the pitch. Yet if Ngumoha grabbed the eye, Trey Nyoni may have been even better. That matters, because hype around academy talent is cheap. Production is what counts. Nyoni gave Liverpool exactly that, with a mature midfield display full of composure, volume and defensive graft. Andoni Iraola praised him afterwards, and Ngumoha was just as clear in his assessment. Trey Nyoni performance backed by numbers Nyoni’s night was built on involvement. He recorded 86 touches, more than any other player on the pitch, and attempted 76 passes. Of those, 65 found their target. The long passing still needs polishing, he completed only one of seven attempts, but the important point is that he kept looking forward. Seven passes into the final third tells its own story. This was not safe football. It was progressive football. There is also a tendency to pigeonhole young midfielders too early. Nyoni does not yet look like an out-and-out creator and he did not register a chance created in this game. Fine. Not every strong midfield display needs a highlight-reel assist attached to it. What he did offer was control, tempo and defensive reliability. He made six defensive contributions, including two tackles and four interceptions. He won three of his six ground duels and came out on top in his only aerial duel. For a 19-year-old in a high-level game, that is substance, not noise. Photo: IMAGO Rio Ngumoha praise says plenty Ngumoha did not hold back when discussing his team-mate. “Trey is top. You guys haven’t even seen him at his top, top level,” he said. “He still has definitely another level to go and he’s only 19. The sky is the limit for Trey and I’m really happy that he’s getting the minutes that he can to show himself, and also show everyone else how good he is. Yeah, he’s top.” That quote stands out because it comes from another teenager who knows exactly what elite potential looks like around him every day. Ngumoha himself has generated serious excitement, and with good reason. His first-half display against Chelsea had pace, bravery and intent. He attacked defenders and played with the kind of personality Liverpool want from wide players. Liverpool youth development looks serious The broader point is simple. Liverpool do not appear to be handing minutes to Ngumoha and Nyoni for sentimental reasons. They are playing because they are good enough to impact games now. There is already a growi

item.title: Brewers manager Pat Murphy’s Jake Bauers free agency warning shades ‘horses**t’ Yankees team’
item.description: Jeff Curry-Imagn Images Brewers manager Pat Murphy’s Jake Bauers free agency warning shades ‘horses**t’ Yankees team’ appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Milwaukee Brewers manager Pat Murphy led his team to a World Series victory . Milwaukee won its first championship on Wednesday after defeating the Tampa Bay Rays in five games in the Fall Classic. Jake Bauers — who is set to enter MLB free agency — played a significant role throughout the season for the Brewers. A moment on the field after the game captured Murphy’s message for Bauers — and the message also shaded the New York Yankees . It was shared by Spectrum News 1 Wisconsin. Jake Bauers gives Pat Murphy the last out ball. #Brewers #WorldSeries #WinOurWay #ThisIsMyCrew pic.twitter.com/E3pblrbzf8 Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) — Spectrum News 1 Wisconsin (@SpectrumNews1WI) October 29, 2026 “Just remember, when you’re on that horses**t Yankees team and you guys are all playing for yourselves, just remember this is the way we used to do it,” Murphy told Bauers. Of course, it isn’t uncommon for star players to have big contract seasons with a small-market team such as the Brewers and go on to sign with a big-market ball club like New York. It will be interesting to see if Bauers will think twice before signing with the Yankees specifically — if New York displays interest in him — after hearing Murphy’s message. Bauers hit .266 with an .874 OPS and 26 home runs during the regular season. He made a big impact in the postseason as well despite an up and down World Series, as Bauers won the National League Championship Series MVP. The left-handed slugger has certainly earned the opportunity to experience free agency and land a lucrative contract. Given how much success he found in Milwaukee, though, one has to wonder if the Brewers will attempt to re-sign him. item.title: Cowboys deliver against Eagles: Who stepped up and who fell short?
item.description: The Cowboys delivered a statement victory against the Philadelphia Eagles , giving fans something to celebrate taking down one of their biggest rivals 38-21 on Monday Night Football. Although every win against the Eagles carries inherent significance, this performance deserves a closer look as more than a handful of Cowboys stepped up when their team needed them. Cornerback Joey Porter Jr. continues to erase opposing receivers when matched up mano a mano. Receivers CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens also stood out, carving up an Eagles defensive backfield filled with Pro Bowl and All-Pro players. From standout individual performances to unexpected developments that could shape the weeks ahead, the biggest winners and losers from the Cowboys victory in Philadelphia offer plenty to unpack. Winner - RB Javonte Williams The Cowboys were criticized for their lack of commitment to the run game but against the Eagles, Dallas shifted their philosophy allowing for running back Javonte Williams to turn in a career day. His 25 carries against Philly was the most times he's ever carried the ball in the NFL while his 155 rushing yards were also a career-high besting his previous mark by 20 yards . His 2-yard TD run with just over two minutes remaining in the fourth quarter tied him for the NFL lead with eight TD scores. Javonte Williams had the best rushing game of his NFL career running all over the Eagles on Monday night. 25 CAR, 155 RUYDS, 1 TD, 6.2 YPC vs Eagles Dallas finished with a season high 204 rushing yards in the 38 to 21 win. pic.twitter.com/plP1jdI8Bi — Football Performances (@NFLPerformances) October 27, 2026 Midway through his second season in Dallas, Williams has already accumulated 19 rushing touchdowns and three receiving scores. Not bad for a player who initially signed a one-year, $3 million dollar deal to come to Dallas. The Cowboys eventually gave him a three-year, $24 million extension . Williams averaged 6.2 yards per carry against Philadelphia and now ranks 12th in rushing with 472 yards, but is only six yards shy of being in the top 10 in that category. In terms of average annual salary, he is the 20th highest paid player at his position makes Williams one of the best value contracts in Dallas and the biggest winner this week. Loser Brian Schottenheimer Dallas head coach Brian Schotteneheimer was under fire from Cowboys Nation after declaring himself an elite play caller and on the surface, putting up 38 points against a Vic Fangio led defense may be enough evidence to support his claim. While his play calling is debatable, his game management on the other hand has had some head-scratching moments. With :43 seconds before halftime and armed with two timeouts, quarterback Dak Prescott found CeeDee Lamb for a 14-yard pickup giving Dallas 1st and 10 at the Eagles 39-yard line. Instead of using a timeout, Dallas rushed to the line where Prescott found Lamb again for a 20-yard gain. Unfortunately for the Cowboys, that left them with only 12

item.title: New turf in five days - Munich stadium chief relaxed over NFL changes
item.description: FILE PHOTO - A general view of Allianz Arena during the National Football League NFL American Football match between Carolina Panthers and New York Giants. (is associated with: «New turf in five days - Munich stadium chief relaxed over NFL changes») Sven Hoppe/dpa Allianz Arena managing director Jürgen Muth has said he is confident that the turf swap after next month's NFL game can be done in time, despite a tight schedule. After the NFL game in Munich on November 15 between the New England Patriots and the Detroit Lions, workers have only five days to replace the hybrid playing surface with grass before Bayern Munich are back in action in the Bundesliga. "We know that this will work in the short timeframe," Muth told a news conference on Thursday, acknowledging that the process will still be a "challenge." The American Football league is visiting Munich for the third time after 2022 and 2024. Changing the turf before the NFL game is by contrast "relatively relaxed," the stadium boss said. After Bayern's Bundesliga clash against Borussia Dortmund this Saturday, organizers have two full weeks to transform the pitch and stadium into an NFL arena.

item.title: England end miserable tri-series on a high with win over Sri Lanka after Ben Duckett heroics
item.description: Ben Duckett struck a sparkling 167 off 132 balls at the Gaddafi Stadium as England finally claimed a win in their tri-series in Pakistan, beating Sri Lanka by 55 runs in a dead rubber. It was Duckett's second hundred in succession and his third in four innings in Lahore , a ground where he also made his previous ODI best. Tom Banton contributed 74 at the top of the order as England piled up 386 for five. The victory was England's first in seven ODIs in Pakistan, after they had chances to win all three previous matches and squandered seemingly unlosable positions in their last two. England had failed to defend 429 against the same opponents last Thursday, and Pavan Rathnayake's second successive century against Harry Brook's side might have brought on a case of deja vu. But Rathnayake lacked support from his middle-order colleagues. Ben Duckett hit another majestic century (PA Wire) When he sliced a sweep off Liam Dawson to depart for a majestic 118 off 77 balls, the eighth wicket to fall, the writing was on the wall. Sri Lanka were all out for 331. While their bid to simulate tournament conditions for next year's World Cup fell flat, England at least head to Australia for a white-ball series with a morale-boosting win. Sent in after losing the toss, England's openers got off to a flyer on Thursday with a 163-run stand. Banton's slash at his first delivery bounced in front of first slip, but England's openers soon got on top from the moment Duckett clipped off his legs then pulled Dilshan Madushanka for back-to-back fours in the second over. Banton was fluent off the back foot and charged slow left-armer Dunith Wellalage and part-timer Janith Liyanage for sixes down the ground. Duckett especially relied on crisp timing and methodical placement to stockpile boundaries. They each went to their fifties at better than a run-a-ball. Banton dragged Dasun Shanaka's off-cutter on to his stumps for 74, but Duckett soon brought up his sixth ODI century off just 89 deliveries. Brook promoted himself to number three and took 12 singles from his first 22 balls following his elevation. Pavan Rathnayake hit another century for Sri Lanka (Reuters) Although he belted two fours and two sixes off his next four deliveries, he botched an attempted scoop to give Asitha Fernando a return catch and depart for 44. Duckett took 29 balls to go from 100 to 150 and went past his previous ODI high of 165, which came at this ground in last year's Champions Trophy, before failing to beat the short fine-leg fielder on the sweep. Will Jacks, Jordan Cox and Sam Curran were all shuffled up the order, relegating Joe Root, and they all contributed decent cameos. England were soon under the pump with the ball despite Sonny Baker bowling Kamindu Mendis through the gate. Baker dropped Avishka Fernando on five while Kusal Mendis had his bat broken, but the Sri Lanka pair put on 84 without looking troubled. Fernando took 13 off Henry Crocombe's first over but holed out for 48. Kusal, run-o

item.title: Skubala gives updates on Bristol City strikers ahead of Bolton
item.description: Skubala gives updates on Bristol City strikers ahead of Bolton Bristol City boss Michael Skubala has confirmed Lorent Tolaj faces a late fitness test ahead of Saturday’s trip to Bolton Wanderers. Tolaj returned to the Robins squad against Stoke City after missing the previous three games, but suffered a heavy blow to his hip following a collision with goalkeeper Viktor Johansson. “He got a big whack on Saturday,” Skubala said. “So he’s got a late fitness test for this Saturday. It’s nothing long-term, but he’s got a contusion on his hip. “He got whacked by the keeper, so it’s a massive bruise. He’s missed quite a lot of training this week, but again, it will be a late call if he makes it for Saturday.” Luke McNally is also continuing to build his fitness, but Elijah Adebayo is set to miss the next couple of games with a quad strain. “Elijah Adebayo is probably going to miss the next couple of games,” Skubala said. “We’ll see whether he makes Saturday or doesn’t make it before the next window. “He’s had a little bit of a strain; we’ve had that scanned and looked at, so he’s going to be out for the foreseeable. “He came off the pitch after Sheffield United with a quad strain. We thought he might recover quite quickly, but he’s going to need a bit more time. “I think the rest of the squad’s looking good and healthy.” There was more positive news on Rob Dickie, who has returned to training after five weeks out. “Rob’s back in, which is great news,” Skubala said. “We’ll see whether he’s available for Saturday. He’s been out five weeks, and he’s been with the team today for the first time. “We’ll see how that looks for Saturday.” Meanwhile, Noah Eile is continuing his recovery from a recent illness. “Noah’s still poorly. He’s still not available,” Skubala said. “He’s definitely heading in the right direction now,” Skubala told Bristol Live . “We’ve got a good grip of it. He’s been quite poorly, so naturally when you’re quite poorly, you lose a bit of weight and all the things you expect from being ill, but we’re definitely on the right side of it.”

item.title: Jamie Redknapp blasts 'aggressive' Mikel Arteta for public dressing down of Arsenal wonderkid Max Dowman
item.description: Fleetwood Town v Arsenal - Carabao Cup Fourth Round - Getty Images Sport Jamie Redknapp has strongly criticised Mikel Arteta for his aggressive touchline reaction towards Max Dowman following the teenager's red card against Fleetwood Town. He insisted that the Arsenal manager should have waited until the dressing room to confront the young forward. Arsenal suffer shock Carabao Cup exit Arsenal suffered a shock Carabao Cup exit on Tuesday, crashing out on penalties to League Two side Fleetwood Town following a 1-1 draw . The major talking point from the match, however, was a late red card for 16-year-old Dowman . The Arsenal forward was dismissed for violent conduct in the 86th minute after kicking out at Harrison Neal. Dowman reacted in the heat of the moment after the Fleetwood midfielder caught him with a heavy challenge from behind. As Dowman left the pitch, Arteta was seen speaking sternly to the teenager on the edge of his technical area. This touchline interaction has since drawn significant criticism from former Liverpool midfielder Redknapp. Redknapp criticises aggressive touchline reaction Redknapp believes Arteta’s reaction was entirely over the top for a young player. He argued that any disciplinary discussions should always take place behind closed doors. "I don’t think you can do that," Redknapp said on The Overlap . "That has to go back in the dressing room, you have to wait. It was a very aggressive manner towards him. Just say nothing. They should have put that game to bed before 85 minutes anyway." Redknapp defends the young Arsenal forward While criticising Arteta, Redknapp showed sympathy for Dowman's sudden loss of composure. He felt that Neal was somewhat fortunate to escape punishment for the initial tackle that sparked the retaliation. "It was a dangerous tackle," Redknapp added. "In our day, you’d just go, 'What a tackle', you’d be celebrating that one. Every time you hook a player, you’re just risking hurting their knee and I suppose Dowman has just reacted." Arsenal look ahead to Liverpool clash Arsenal have launched an official appeal against Dowman’s sending off. If the red card is upheld, the teenager will serve a three-match suspension, ruling him out of Premier League fixtures against Liverpool, Hull City, and Newcastle. The club must quickly move on from one of the biggest upsets in Carabao Cup history. Arteta’s men travel to Anfield on Sunday for a massive Premier League showdown with Liverpool. Arsenal currently sit second in the league table after eight matches. They are only behind current leaders Manchester City on goal difference.

item.title: ‘We’re about to make Pittsburgh ours’: Browns star who called Steelers ‘dirty’ sends another message
item.description: Aug 8, 2025; Charlotte, North Carolina, USA; Cleveland Browns helmet during the first quarter against the Carolina Panthers at Bank of America Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jim Dedmon-Imagn Images The Pittsburgh Steelers fell 27-24 to the Cleveland Browns in Week 4, and Browns defensive lineman Jared Verse made it clear after the game that he felt the Steelers played dirty. On Sunday, the teams will rematch, as the Browns travel to the Steel City to determine which team will sit atop the AFC North heading into Week 9. After their first meeting, Browns defensive lineman Jared Verse asserted that he felt the Steelers played dirty during the game. “I was talking to them crazy. I was telling them, ‘You’re double-teaming, y’all sliding, y’all garbage.’ I don’t got no respect for anybody that plays too dirty and does too much extra s*** after the game,” Verse said. “I can’t wait to see them again. It’s going to be a good time when I see them again.” Steelers stalwart Cam Heyward responded on Tuesday’s episode of The Rich Eisen Show. “Double teaming, sliding, chipping, are those not allowed in our game? Yeah, I got the bruises to prove it. But we don’t whine about it, baby. It’s part of the game,” Heyward said. On Thursday, the story took its next step, with Verse acknowledging Heyward’s comments and sending a message of his own. “Same as always, I’m just going in there ready to dominate. Obviously I’ve been waiting for this one for a little bit,” Verse told reporters.via Scott Petrak on X. Browns DE Jared Verse said he’s been waiting for rematch with Steelers, not worried about what Cam Hayward said. https://t.co/xs0BRzryND — Scott Petrak ct (@ScottPetrak) October 29, 2026 “The whole bulletin board material and things like that. I’m just ready to go put them hands on…I’m not worried about their O-line, I’m not worried about nobody on they team. We out there to go dominate. We’re about to make Pittsburgh ours on Sunday.” Sunday’s contest will be the most important regular-season game between the teams since 1994, as the Steelers look to avoid the first sweep at Cleveland’s hands since 1988. item.title: T.C. Taylor makes offensive strategy change following Bethune-Cookman loss
item.description: T.C. Taylor makes offensive strategy change following Bethune-Cookman loss appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . After Jackson State’s shocking loss to Bethune-Cookman , T.C. Taylor is set to make official strategy changes in their next game against Mississippi Valley State, after a bye week. Taylor said he plans to be more involved in the offense. “Just being a little more involved myself. The last couple of years, I’ve been taking a backseat to a lot of the play-calling. I’ve got to be a little more involved with it. And I’m going to do that this week.” Statistically, Jackson State is still one of the best offenses in the SWAC. They rank number four in scoring offense, averaging 35.6 points per game, and they’re in the top five in total offense, rushing offense, and passing offense. But the Bethune-Cookman game saw them generate only 244 yards of total offense and 33 rushing yards on 36 attempts. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Taylor says he plans to use the bye week to reset as they enter a tough stretch of the schedule. “I like when we get to a bye week. I like to go back and look at all the plays we’ve run and things we can do for each player, the guys that we’re really counting on in these situations.” He also specifically pinpointed ways that they can deal with different defensive coverages, specifically ones where the defense is pressuring the pass game. “Find ways to attack a lot of pressure, find ways to attack maybe if they’re playing a lot of quarters and things like that,” Taylor said. Jackson State faces in-state rival Mississippi Valley on November 7. item.title: Athletic: Chelsea star planning to return “earlier than planned” from horror injury
item.description: Athletic: Chelsea star planning to return “earlier than planned” from horror injury Emi Martinez is pushing for a speedy return from the broken jaw he suffered against Everton two weeks ago. If you enjoy Talk Chelsea coverage and want to see more of it, add us as a preferred source on Google to make us a favourite and see more of our content. Since Emi Martinez’s horrific collision with Jarrad Branthwaite in the Everton game two weeks ago, the focus was been on whether he’s ok, and then on how Mike Penders will do as his replacement. There hasn’t been much information about how soon the Argentine could be back, until today’s report from the Athletic. Martinez pushes for early return after jaw surgery Emi Martinez post-surgery Simon Johnson says that the goalkeeper is planning to “make an earlier than planned return,” after surgery on his broken jaw. Martinez himself said he would be “back in a few weeks,” which was taken to mean a month at least. But sources “with knowledge of his rehabilitation” have told Johnson that he could now “return sooner than that time frame.” We still wouldn’t expect to see him in the next week, and beyond that there is an international break. It feels eminently more sensible to just wait until after that, but Martinez isn’t that sort of character. He will be pushing to get back out there as soon as he has clearance, no matter whether it’s sensible or not. He will almost certainly be wearing one of those Abraham Lincoln jaw protectors. In other news… Xabi Alonso’s comments about the importance of the Carabao Cup have not been well received by Chelsea fans. Emmanuel Emegha got his first competitive minutes for Chelsea last night, and could play an important role on Saturday. Alonso didn’t bring on Estevao for even a minute in the game, and had to answer questions about that afterwards.

item.title: Suns rumors: Why there’s growing frustration in locker room after just 3 games
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Suns rumors: Why there’s growing frustration in locker room after just 3 games appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Frustration is reportedly building inside the Phoenix Suns ’ locker room just three games into the season. The concern centers on the team’s lack of a traditional point guard, an issue that has complicated Phoenix’s offensive organization despite its plans to develop Jalen Green ’s playmaking. NBA insider Chris Haynes revealed the growing concerns during NBA TV’s Hayne Headlines segment. His reporting suggests the Suns are struggling to establish a consistent offensive structure despite having several talented structure despite having several talented scorers. “What I found out was that there’s some growing frustration within that locker room,” Haynes said in a video shared on X. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Haynes explained that Phoenix lacks a player capable of consistently organizing possessions and creating quality opportunities for teammates. The Suns have relied on Devin Booker alongside Jalen Green and Dillon Brooks. However, none of those players primarily operate as a traditional pass-first point guard. “You don’t have a true traditional point guard that can get everybody, give everybody looks, and get everything organized,” Haynes explained. The concern comes after Booker’s difficult performance against the Oklahoma City Thunder on Monday. He scored just three points while shooting 1-of-7 from the field. Haynes also noted that Phoenix ranks in the bottom half of the NBA in team assists, reflecting its early offensive difficulties. Despite the reported frustration, there is no indication that the Suns are immediately pursuing a roster change. “I don’t know that the Suns are looking to address [it] as of now,” Haynes said. Instead, Phoenix reportedly hopes to distribute playmaking responsibilities among multiple players. The team’s offensive struggles have already prompted concerns about its early-season performance. item.title: “Cooper Flagg For MVP Don’t Get It Twisted” – Mavericks Fans On Cloud Nine After ROY’s Surgical Performance Leads to Blowout Win Over Thunder
item.description: Cooper Flagg © X/ @dallasmavs Cooper Flagg’s stellar start this season continued on Wednesday as he led the Dallas Mavericks to a 120-96 win over one of the league’s best defensive units , the OKC Thunder. Flagg torched the 2025 NBA champions with a surgical offensive performance, scoring 26 points and dishing eight assists without a turnover. Flagg also grabbed five rebounds. The box score didn’t show it, but the reigning Rookie of the Year also had a solid defensive shift. After Flagg’s 26-8 game against the Thunder, his season averages improved to 25.3 points, 5.3 rebounds, 6.8 assists, 2.8 steals and 1.3 blocks per game in four appearances. The numbers could have been even better had he not left Friday’s 121-105 win over the Indiana Pacers with a contact injury. In that game, Flagg had 14 points, five rebounds, six assists and three steals in just 17 minutes. As Flagg looks better with each game, Mavericks fans rallied behind him as not just an All-Star and All-NBA candidate, but also an MVP candidate. “COOPER FLAGG FOR MVP DON’T GET IT TWISTED ‼️” one fan said. Why Cooper Flagg can actually be in the conversation for MVP Whether Cooper Flagg wins MVP or not is a long shot. He’s only 19, and no one in history has achieved this milestone at that age. However, Flagg can be in that conversation. Granted, a four-game sample size is small to make such predictions, but Flagg has looked like one of the most NBA-ready prospects in recent memory. The Mavericks also developed him well in his rookie year. Former coach Jason Kidd deserves credit, as he put Flagg in uncomfortable positions and polished a few areas of his game, especially his playmaking skills as a point guard. Flagg has also gotten stronger, improving his play-finishing and ability to get to his spots. Even some of the league’s top defenders, Giannis Antetokounmpo, Aaron Nesmith and Amen Thompson, couldn’t slow him down. Flagg’s two-way versatility as a 6-foot-10 forward is rare, so he’s likely to maintain his current averages the rest of the year. If that also translates into a potential top-four finish, Flagg will have a case as an MVP candidate, as the Mavericks aren’t widely projected to make the playoffs. In terms of competition, voters might be fatigued to nominate Shai Gilgeous-Alexander for MVP for a third straight year. Luka Doncic might have the best case to win his first. Nikola Jokic’s Nuggets are off to a slow start, and he’s not been at his best either. Giannis Antetokounmpo was another MVP favorite, but after a 1-4 start, it seems Miami has a lot to figure out chemistry-wise. item.title: Savion Williams, Darren Waller, And More Must-Start Fantasy Football Bench Players For Week 8
item.description: Green Bay Packers wide receiver Savion Williams (83) carries the ball during the second quarter against the Detroit Lions at Ford Field. Mandatory Credit: Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Every week we have players sitting on our bench who we consider starting, but it's hard to pull the trigger on. We are going to take a look at some of those players who might be sitting on your bench this week. These are the fantasy football bench players you should consider starting in Week 8. QB Kyler Murray, Minnesota Vikings Murray hasn't been great so far this season for fantasy owners. Through five games, he has racked up just 812 yards, three touchdowns, and two interceptions, while rushing for 132 scoreless yards. If he can't break out this week, then it might never happen, but we have high hopes. In Week 8, the Vikings go up against the Detroit Lions, who have allowed the most fantasy points to quarterbacks this season. They are allowing 26.2 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks. This will be the game that Murray finally plays up to his abilities in Minnesota. If he doesn't have a big game this week, he should be cast to the waiver wire for the remainder of the year. RB Mike Washington Jr, Las Vegas Raiders Ashton Jeanty is clearly not healthy, and it has shown in both his production and playing time. It has become a near split backfield in Las Vegas, with Jeanty being ineffective. The Raiders refuse to rest their star running back, and it has taken a toll on his production and efficiency. Washington will continue to see an increased role while Jeanty struggles through injury. He could see double-digit opportunities again in Week 8 for the third time in the past five weeks. That's enough to make him a solid starting option against the New York Jets, who are a slightly above-average matchup. WR Savion Williams, Green Bay Packers Matthew Golden is expected to play tonight, but he heads into the game banged up on a short week with multiple injuries. Williams has seen his utilization increase over the past few weeks, and this could be his best game yet. Over the past two weeks, he has caught all seven of his targets for 79 yards and carried the ball four times for 13 more yards. They are figuring out ways to get the ball into his hands, and we expect that to continue tonight. With 11 opportunities in two weeks, the playmaker is worth considering as a flex option. TE Darren Waller, Carolina Panthers Waller has been a bit of a boom-or-bust option this season. Last week, he caught a 50-yard touchdown pass, and the week before he put up a goose egg. However, he has massive upside and has caught three touchdowns in six games this season for 198 yards. Even in a tough matchup against the Packers, he is capable of making big plays and finding the end zone. item.title: ‘Come on, referee’ – Ex-PGMOL chief calls out Darren England over one incident in Liverpool win
item.description: ‘Come on, referee’ – Ex-PGMOL chief calls out Darren England over one incident in Liverpool win Darren England has been criticised for not issuing a yellow card in response to one contentious incident in Liverpool’s Carabao Cup tie against Chelsea on Wednesday night. The referee booked four players over the course of the match at Anfield, but he didn’t reach for his pocket when Emmanuel Emegha inexplicably charged at Virgil van Dijk off the ball and shoved the Reds captain to the ground . The veteran defender shrugged off questions about that incident afterwards, although a former chief executive of the PGMOL (now Pro Ref) believes that the Blues striker should’ve been cautioned for his indiscetion. Hackett: England should’ve booked Emegha Speaking to Football Insider , Keith Hackett said: “Virgil van Dijk had every right to be annoyed with the referee and his opponent. The referee took no action for what was a very aggressive run and push that met the criteria for being reckless. “Van Dijk ended up on the floor, so this player is very fortunate not to receive a yellow card. Come on referee, you had a reasonable game, but you could have done better here. “This could have easily caused a mass confrontation. I am surprised and disappointed that a yellow card was not issued to the Chelsea player.” Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust Emegha was lucky to avoid a yellow card Hackett is right – Emegha was fortunate to avoid a yellow card for his shove on Van Dijk, especially considering some of the bookings that England handed out earlier in the match. For example, Lewis Koumas was harshly cautioned after just 10 minutes for a minor foul on Maxence Lacroix, which was far less of an indiscretion than what the Chelsea substitute did to his fellow Dutchman in the second half. There was no discernible reason for the Blues attacker to run at the Liverpool captain and barge him to the ground, and as Hackett said, it could easily have led to a large-scale brawl between players from both teams. We don’t want to see cards being dished out unnecessarily, but Emegha’s petulance would have deserved a booking, certainly more so than Koumas for his foul on Lacroix.

item.title: Steelers’ Mike McCarthy provides encouraging injury news
item.description: Sep 27, 2026; Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, USA; Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver Roman Wilson (14) celebrates with wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr. (11) and center Zach Frazier (54) after a touchdown during the first quarter against the Cincinnati Bengals at Acrisure Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Barry Reeger-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Steelers currently have seven players on injured reserve, including some of the team’s top wide receivers and defensive linemen. And according to Pittsburgh head coach Mike McCarthy, every eligible name has a chance at a return this season. “Thinking through the list, I think all those guys have a chance to come back,” McCarthy told the media Thursday. The lone exception, of course, would be defensive lineman Logan Lee, who was placed on season-ending IR before cutdown day in August. Currently, Pittsburgh’s injured reserve list features the following players: WR Roman Wilson (placed on IR Oct. 17) WR Michael Pittman Jr. (placed on IR Oct. 10) DL Derrick Harmon (placed on IR Oct. 5) DL Sebastian Joseph-Day (placed on IR Oct. 22) DL Logan Lee (placed on IR Aug. 13) OL Gennings Dunker (placed on IR Sept. 26) OL Jack Driscoll (placed on IR Aug. 30) NFL teams can bring players from IR to the 53-man roster up to eight times in the regular season per league rules. Pittsburgh has already used up two of those opportunities with safety Deshon Elliott making his Steelers return last week and Driscoll being designated to return after being placed on IR on cutdown day. However, Pittsburgh can still bring back the other five eligible names currently on the list once they miss their minimum of four games. Dunker and Driscoll could see their 21-day practice periods open at any point. Harmon and Pittman can start to return after the Steelers-Browns matchup on Nov. 1 if healthy.

item.title: Has Paige Spiranac Has Completely Changed Golf?
item.description: Aug 21, 2025; Atlanta, Georgia, USA; Reporter Paige Spiranac on the first hole during the first round of the TOUR Championship golf tournament. Mandatory Credit: Brett Davis-Imagn Images Paige Spiranac might not be competing on the LPGA Tour, but she’s arguably one of the most recognizable personalities in golf. And that continues to bother some traditional golf fans. Spiranac has built a massive following through social media, combining golf instruction, entertainment, and her outspoken personality to reach an audience far beyond the sport’s traditional fan base. But her popularity has also sparked criticism from those who believe golf should be more focused on competition than social media influence. Here’s the reality: Spiranac has found a way to make golf relevant to people who might otherwise never watch a tournament. Whether fans love her content or criticize her approach, there’s no denying the attention she brings to the game. The bigger question is whether golf’s traditional audience is willing to embrace personalities who grow the sport differently. Paige Spiranac isn’t ruining golf. She might be exposing just how outdated some of its traditions really are.

item.title: Kimi Antonelli absent from Mexican Grand Prix media day ahead of F1 title coronation
item.description: Kimi Antonelli will miss media day at the Mexican Grand Prix on Thursday due to a viral illness. Antonelli needs to finish ninth or higher to guarantee the world championship this Sunday in Mexico City and, even if he finishes outside the points, George Russell or Lewis Hamilton must win the race to extend the title race to Brazil next week. Yet off the back of his impressive win in Austin last Sunday, his ninth grand prix triumph of the season, 20-year-old Antonelli is suffering from illness and has been excused from fulfilling his mandatory media duties from the FIA on Thursday. However, Mercedes do expect Antonelli to be fit and ready to go for Friday’s two practice sessions at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez. A short Mercedes statement read: “Kimi is feeling under the weather today as he recovers from a viral illness. “As a precaution, the FIA have excused him from his mandatory media duties to give him the chance to rest head of the weekend. “We expect him to be back tomorrow.” Antonelli, who is set to become the sport’s youngest-ever champion, has a 123-point lead over teammate Russell with 125 points left on the table. The Italian is only in his second season in the sport, having replaced Lewis Hamilton at Mercedes last year. Only Hamilton and Jacques Villeneuve have previously won the world championship in their second season. The race on Sunday starts at 8pm GMT.

item.title: LSU’s Lane Kiffin supports 24-team College Football Playoff
item.description: The 2026 college football season is set to be the final one with the 12-team College Football Playoff. ESPN and the CFP are nearing a deal to expand to 24 teams, starting in 2027. It’s sparked mixed reactions across the college football community, and now, LSU head coach Lane Kiffin has given his take. MORE: Predicting SEC football scores in Week 9: Florida looks to keep momentum vs. Georgia In Kiffin’s mind, it “had to happen.” “I think it had to happen,” Kiffin said on the “Brandon Walker College Football Show.” “You could say, okay, 12 is better, but not when you take into account the way college football is set up now. The conferences are so different. The four conferences. They are. They’re different stadiums, they’re different environments, they’re different middle to bottom of them, and so you’re not playing equal schedules; they’re not even close. “If you took an SEC team and gave them another one of those conference’s schedules, they’d average two more wins. Well, that’s a big deal. So, I say all that to say you had to go to more teams, because the system’s broke in how they pick them, and nothing against the committee.” It should also be mentioned that an expanded playoff would help the SEC, so it’s not surprising to see Kiffin be in favor of it. His team will have an even better chance of making it to the CFP. LSU’s next game Sep 26, 2026; Baton Rouge, Louisiana, USA; LSU Tigers head coach Lane Kiffin reacts during the second quarter against the Texas A&M Aggies at Tiger Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Stephen Lew-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) LSU is 6-2 overall and has what is basically a “playoff elimination” game next Saturday (Nov. 7) against Alabama. The loser will have three losses and be up a creek for the rest of the season. item.description: In the lead-up to the Ocarina of Time ’s Switch 2 remake , I’ve spent a lot of time trying to nail down what makes the Legend of Zelda series so special. You could chalk a lot of its success up to pure design, as Nintendo has hammered out how to create a grand adventure game, whether it's working with pixels or an enormous 3D world. But any technical explanation for Zelda’s enduring success feels too cold and mechanical for a series that radiates warmth and joy; it simply doesn’t communicate how it feels to get lost in a Zelda game.

item.title: 2027: Makinde pledges to revive South-East industries
item.description: …Promises to tackle 25% interest rates, expand long-term financing By Chinedu Adonu ENUGU — The presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Seyi Makinde, has pledged to tackle high interest rates and improve access to long-term financing to revive industries, expand businesses and create jobs in the South-East if elected president in 2027. Makinde, the Oyo State governor, made the pledge during a town hall meeting with stakeholders from the region in Enugu, where he identified manufacturing as a critical driver of economic growth, employment and poverty reduction. He said the South-East’s economic potential extended beyond trading to industrial production, particularly in commercial and manufacturing centres such as Onitsha and Nnewi in Anambra State. According to him, businesses cannot expand production or employ millions of Nigerians when interest rates remain high and long-term credit facilities are difficult to access. “Yes, trading is something this zone is synonymous with, but so is manufacturing. If you go to Onitsha and Nnewi, you will discover that the South-East is not just about trading; manufacturing is also thriving here. “You cannot expand manufacturing and employ millions of people when interest rates are at 25 per cent and long-term financing facilities are unavailable. These are two challenges we will tackle decisively,” he said. Makinde said his proposed economic reforms would shift Nigeria away from dependence on the sharing of federal allocations towards production, industrial expansion and wealth creation. “The responsibility of government is to create a conducive environment for businesses to thrive. That is precisely what we will do. We will create an enabling environment for businesses to flourish throughout the country,” he said. Drawing on his private-sector experience, the governor said access to long-term financing was essential for economic expansion, arguing that Nigeria’s financial system remained dominated by short-term loans largely suited to trading. “I come from the private sector. I started paying workers’ salaries at the age of 29, and now I am 58. I have been paying salaries from then until today, so I understand when an economy is expanding. “One indication of an expanding economy is the availability of long-term financing within the economic system. Right now, bankers can tell you that what we have been experiencing is mainly short-term financing facilities meant for trading,” he said. He said expanding manufacturing would help address unemployment, particularly among young people, and pledged to support entrepreneurs capable of creating sustainable jobs. Makinde cited the commissioning of the headquarters of Capital Sage, a conglomerate in Ibadan, as an example of the employment opportunities businesses could generate when given the right conditions to grow. Beyond industrial development, the APM candidate said his economic agenda would prioritise skills acquisition to improve young people

item.title: 2027: Tinubu lacks energy to govern, Obi says
item.description: …Urges South-East to shun ethnic politics By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki ABAKALIKI — The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has questioned President Bola Tinubu’s competence and energy to govern Nigeria, urging him to leave office and rest. Obi spoke at an NDC town hall and stakeholders’ meeting held at the Citi-Hub Centre, Mile 50, Abakaliki, Ebonyi State, where he urged Nigerians to unite behind candidates based on their qualifications and capacity to deliver good governance rather than ethnic considerations. He cautioned the South-East against division, insisting that voters in Ebonyi and other parts of the country should support him based on his credentials, not because he is Igbo. “Let nobody divide the South-East. I don’t want the people of Ebonyi to vote for me because I am from the South-East. I don’t want you to vote for me because I am an Igbo person. “My dear people, I want you to vote for me because I am qualified to be the President of this country. I want you to vote for me because I am the leading candidate,” he said. The former Anambra State governor challenged Tinubu to explain his administration’s record over the past three years, particularly the use of funds borrowed by the Federal Government. “I want President Tinubu to come to Abakaliki to tell the people what he has done in the past three years. I want him to come to Abakaliki to tell you what he used the money he has been borrowing to do for the past three years,” Obi said. He also questioned the President’s reported time spent outside Nigeria, arguing that he should be able to travel across the country to account for his administration’s performance. “President Tinubu does not have the competence to run Nigeria. He does not have the energy to run Nigeria. He should pack his things, go home and rest,” Obi said. Outlining his proposed priorities if elected president in 2027, Obi said his administration would declare emergencies in key sectors, including national unity, security, education, healthcare, corruption and food production. On national unity, he said his government would seek to reduce ethnic divisions and ensure that appointments reflected the federal character principle. “We must unite this country. Our pride should not be consideration of employment, this or that. We will operate federal character for all the jobs we have. So, we must unite the country,” he said. On security, Obi promised decisive action against insecurity and pledged to equip security agencies to protect lives and property. “We will declare emergency in the security of lives and property in Nigeria. We will deal with insecurity decisively. Nobody will be in charge, we will be in charge,” he said. He specifically promised stronger action against kidnappers targeting schoolchildren, saying his administration would ensure that security agencies pursued those responsible and protected vulnerable communities. “If I am President of this country, kids come to school
