item.title: 'More missions, more often': NASA is overhauling how it selects science missions
item.description: null NASA is overhauling how it selects and develops science missions, with changes intended to reduce costs, streamline competition and get missions into space faster. The new approach, called Competition Model 2.0 (CM 2.0), was announced on Oct. 21 in an open letter from Nicky Fox, associate administrator of NASA's Science Mission Directorate (SMD), to the NASA science community. The changes, directed by NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman, could significantly reshape how scientists, universities, NASA centers and commercial companies vie for future missions. "We have heard you. We have listened. We know that the burden of bringing great ideas forward has been too heavy for too long," Fox stated in the letter. The new process aims to prioritize scientific merit over unduly complicated engineering and financial planning during initial evaluations, and reduce selection timelines to encourage innovation. Fox and other top NASA science officials will provide an overview of the reforms during a virtual town hall today (Oct. 26) at 2 p.m. EDT (1800 GMT). A livestream of the event will be available here , with an opportunity for the public to submit questions here . NASA currently selects many of its science missions through competitive Announcements of Opportunity (AOs), inviting scientists and research institutions to submit proposals. Under the existing two-step process, competing teams must include thorough engineering and financial details as part of their proposals before NASA selects finalists for further study. The process can take almost three years, requiring significant investments of time and resources from teams that may ultimately never get selected. CM 2.0 aims to reduce that burden by emphasizing scientific distinction during initial evaluations, allowing teams to defer much of the engineering and financial planning until later. Instead, initial proposals will focus on the scientific objectives of a mission and a preliminary plan for how to accomplish them. NASA organizes its science missions into different classes based on their size, cost and objectives, with selection procedures varying between them. These range from smaller Explorer missions to large, expensive flagships like the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST). Under CM 2.0, programs including smaller Discovery planetary missions, larger New Frontiers spacecraft and Astro-Probes, a program that focuses on mid-sized astronomy missions, will retain a streamlined version of the existing two-step process, but with nearly half of the material required for initial proposals. "This means that the original 35-months timeline will be reduced to about 19.5 months, all while having a stronger, more mature mission at the time of selection," Fox wrote. Flagship missions, meanwhile, will continue following their current procedures, which were recently revised based on lessons learned from a study of best practices examining the development of JWST. item.title: Beyond the Skyline: How Landmark Waterview Apartment Is Shaping a New Era of Premium Living in Lagos
item.description: With 200-plus live, work and play apartments, panoramic Atlantic views and an established business and leisure destination at its doorstep, Landmark Africa ‘s latest residential development, Landmark Waterview Apartments , is positioning itself as a compelling addition to Lagos’ premium property market. The main value proposition is “ convenience living ”. Lagos has no shortage of ambitious residential developments. Across Victoria Island, Ikoyi and the Lekki corridor, new towers continue to reshape the city’s skyline, competing for the attention of homeowners and investors. Yet, as the premium property market becomes increasingly competitive, the question for developers is no longer simply how high they can build but what lasting value they can offer beyond the apartment itself. For Landmark Africa, the answer lies in a business model it has spent nearly three decades developing. With Landmark Waterview Apartments, the company is bringing residential ownership into one of Lagos’ most established business, leisure, and lifestyle destinations, combining contemporary homes with the commercial activity, hospitality infrastructure, and recreational experiences that have become synonymous with the Landmark brand. The 20-storey development, situated within Landmark Lagos ecosystem in Victoria Island, has apartments overlooking the Atlantic coastline and Lagos skyline. Approximately 40% of the apartments have already been sold, reflecting early market interest in a project that seeks to offer more than conventional apartment ownership. From Commercial Real Estate to Destination Development Landmark Africa’s journey began in 1997 with serviced offices, long before the concept of integrated lifestyle destinations became a prominent feature of Nigeria’s real estate market. Over the years, the company expanded into commercial property, mixed-use developments featuring hospitality, tourism, entertainment, and leisure components, developing a portfolio that reflects an increasingly diversified approach to real estate. Its flagship Landmark Lagos destination became one of the most visible expressions of that strategy. By bringing together corporate offices, event facilities, restaurants, hospitality, retail, andrecreational attractions, the company helped establish a destination that attracted more than four million visitors annually at its peak. The significance of that achievement extends beyond visitor numbers. It demonstrated Landmark’s ability to create and sustain commercial activity by attracting businesses and consumers to a shared destination. Waterview represents an important next step in that evolution: introducing residential ownership into an environment that has already established its commercial and lifestyle appeal. For buyers, this means investing in a property connected to an existing destination rather than relying solely on the promise of future neighbourhood development. item.title: On this day in space! Oct. 25, 1671: Astronomer Giovanni Cassini discovers Iapetus, Saturn's 'yin-yang' moon
item.description: null On Oct. 25, 1671, the Italian astronomer Giovanni Cassini discovered a new moon at Saturn! Iapetus was the second moon anyone had ever found orbiting Saturn, and it was the first of four moons Cassini would discover at the ringed planet. The Dutch astronomer Christiaan Huygens had discovered Titan , the largest of Saturn's moons, about six years earlier. After Cassini found Iapetus, he also found the moons Rhea, Tethys and Dione. When Cassini first saw Iapetus, the moon looked like a tiny speck on the west side of Saturn. He calculated its orbit and thought he would be able to see it again on the east side of Saturn 39 days later, but it was nowhere to be seen. When it reappeared on the west side again, Cassini realized that Iapetus must be darker on one side than the other , which made it harder to see when the dark side was facing Earth. More than 300 years later, NASA sent a spacecraft named Cassini to Saturn, and that Cassini took some pretty awesome photos of Iapetus. Realizing Iapetus kind of resembled a yin-yang, it has since been nicknamed the " yin-yang moon ." This image taken by the Cassini spacecraft shows what the two-tone surface of the moon Iapetus looks like without false color. (Image credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech/Space Science Institute) How it mattered The discovery of Iapetus, with its yin-yang bright and dark hemispheres, has added to our understanding of how moons form. "Using the computer simulations, the researchers concluded ... the inner moons of Saturn and its gorgeous rings are all relatively young. The more distant moons Titan and Iapetus would not have been formed at the same time." "Our best guess is that Saturn had a similar collection of moons before, but their orbits were disturbed by a special kind of orbital resonance involving Saturn's motion around the sun. Eventually, the orbits of neighboring moons crossed, and these objects collided. From this rubble, the present set of moons and rings formed." Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

item.title: October's 'Hunter's Moon' stalks into the autumn sky tonight: Here's what you need to know
item.description: null October's full "Hunter's Moon" treated stargazers to a mesmerizing natural light show when it rose overnight on Oct. 25-26! Check out our wrap article to see the best photos of the October full moon . The October full moon rises tonight! Here's everything you need to know about the "Hunter's Moon," including where to see it, how it got its name and other tricks of the light and mind that could conspire to create a truly spectacular lunar light show. October's moon reaches 100% illumination at 12:12 a.m. EDT (0412 GMT) on Oct. 26, as the lunar disk shines opposite the sun in Earth's sky. The shadowy terminator that separates the day and night side of the moon is conspicuously absent around this time, as are the shadows that throw craters into spectacular relief during the waxing and waning lunar phases. Instead, it's a perfect time to explore the dark lunar "seas" that cover the moon's surface where lava flooded impact basins billions of years ago, before hardening to create enormous basaltic plains. Streaks of reflective material can also be spotted streaking away from bright young craters, where material from the lunar subsurface was excavated and cast across the moon's surface during brutal asteroid impacts. Where and when to see the October full moon. Stargazers in the U.S. will get their first view of the full moon as it climbs into the eastern sky at sunset on Oct. 25. Be sure to check out Time and Date's moonrise tracker to discover the exact timings for your location. The moon often appears particularly large while close to the horizon, thanks to a phenomenon called the "Moon Effect," wherein our brains trick us into thinking that the lunar disk is larger while in close visual proximity to the ground than it is when overhead. The moon can also take on a spectacular yellow-orange color in the hour after moonrise, as blue wavelengths of its reflected light — the shortest in the visible spectrum — are scattered during its oblique passage through Earth's atmosphere . Why is the October full moon called the "Hunter's Moon"? October's full moon is commonly known as the Hunter's Moon in the Northern Hemisphere because it rises soon after farmers have cleared away the summer's harvest, leaving the fields bare for hunters to catch their prey and prepare it as food for the winter, according to the Old Farmer's Almanac . It's also called the "Migrating Moon" by the North American Cree people, in reference to the birds that travel to warmer climates around the time of its rising. The Ojibwe and the Haida know it asthe "Freezing Moon," to reflect the drop in temperature that occurs in autumn. Want to make the most of the October full moon? Then be sure to check out our guide to observing the moon and photographing the lunar disk , along with our picks of the best cameras and lenses for astrophotography . item.description: Veekee James showcasing her custom wine-red corset dress and gold woven box clutch. Veekee James at a party? Trust her to come dressed like the celebration has its own red carpet. And when it’s a Nigerian wedding, with good music, beautiful traditional outfits and guests who take their fashion very seriously, you already know she’s going to have some fun with her look. Yesterday, Afrobeats star Zlatan Ibile , whose real name is Omoniyi Temidayo Raphael , and his partner, Davita Omoniyi , celebrated their traditional wedding with family, friends and some familiar faces from the entertainment industry. Among the guests was Nigerian fashion designer Veekee James, who arrived in a gorgeous wine-red and champagne creation from her own fashion label. And between the sculpted corset, the beaded sleeves and that towering gele, there was so much to admire. Veekee James in a custom wine-red sheer corset dress with metallic sequin detailing and a structured metallic gele. Let’s start with the dress. Veekee chose a floor-length, figure-hugging design featuring a sheer corset-style bodice covered in vertical rows of wine-red crystals. The sweetheart-inspired neckline extended into a high, embellished collar, while the long sheer sleeves featured rows of burgundy beads. The fitted skirt followed a mermaid silhouette, with sweeping patterns of gold sequins, wine-red embroidery and dusty-rose detailing running down to a subtle train. Structural details of the sheer corset bodice, crystal neckband, and sequin wave skirt on Veekee James’ wedding guest dress. And that gele! Veekee went for a tall, fan-pleated design in metallic champagne, giving her look even more height and making the headwrap a fashion moment of its own. She paired it with burgundy drop earrings, a structured gold woven box clutch and soft, neutral makeup that complemented the colours of her outfit. Styling details of Veekee James’ high-neck crystal collar, sheer corset bodice, and pleated metallic gele. Of course, Veekee knows her way around a corset. As the founder and creative director of her eponymous fashion label, she’s known for sculpted silhouettes, detailed beadwork and glamorous occasionwear. For Zlatan and Davita’s wedding, she brought those design elements into her own wardrobe, pairing a fitted, heavily embellished dress with a traditional gele. What we particularly love is how the colours work together. The deep wine-red gives the dress its richness, while the champagne and gold details brighten the overall look. Even with the crystals, beading and high neckline, the accessories have their place, from the matching earrings to the gold clutch. Veekee James posing alongside her husband Femi Atere at Zlatan Ibile and Davita Omoniyi’s wedding. And if you’ve been looking for wedding guest inspiration, Veekee’s outfit offers a lovely styling idea: when your dress has this much detail around the neckline, you can leave out the necklace and let your earrings and gele do their thing. item.title: Zlatan Ibile & Davita Omoniyi Celebrate Yoruba Heritage in Lemon Yellow and Mint Green
item.description: Zlatan Ibile and Davita Omoniyi celebrating their Yoruba cultural heritage during their wedding ceremony. Lemon yellow and mint green? Now that’s a colour combination we can get behind. For their second traditional wedding look, Zlatan Ibile and Davita Omoniyi ( Omoniyi Temidayo Raphael ) have switched things up, trading their earlier burgundy and ivory outfits for a softer palette that feels right at home at a Yoruba wedding. And if you thought one outfit change was enough for this celebration, you know Nigerian weddings better than that! Zlatan Ibile and Davita Omoniyi in custom Mazelle Bridal pastel Yoruba traditional attire, styled by Goodnews Emmanuel Icon. After honouring Davita’s Edo heritage in their first look, the couple are now celebrating Zlatan’s Yoruba roots in coordinated outfits by Mazelle Bridal. Davita wears a custom lemon-yellow gown with a sculpted, corset-style bodice, a sweetheart-inspired neckline and long sleeves with flared cuffs. Mint-green appliqué forms swirling, floral-inspired patterns across the bodice and fitted, floor-length skirt, with gold-toned accents adding extra detail. Davita Omoniyi showcasing her custom Mazelle Bridal outfit for her Yoruba traditional wedding look. She completes the look with a large, pleated lemon-yellow gele and matching sheer fabric draped over her arm. A green statement necklace, matching earrings and a mint-green clutch bring the accessories together, while the soft yellow and green palette gives her bridal look a fresh, coordinated finish. Davita Omoniyi wearing a pleated circular gele and sheer veil for her second traditional wedding outfit change. Zlatan matches her in a custom mint-green agbada by Mazelle Bridal, featuring subtle embroidery across the chest. He finishes his outfit with a structured fila, layers of white beads and a carved green walking stick that picks up the colour of his attire. Zlatan Ibile in a custom Mazelle Bridal Agbada set for his Yoruba traditional wedding. Styled by Goodnews Emmanuel Icon, the couple pose hand in hand against a plum backdrop. Their first look celebrated Davita’s Edo heritage, and this second outfit honours Zlatan’s Yoruba roots, giving their wedding wardrobe two lovely cultural chapters. And with lemon yellow and mint green taking centre stage, this outfit change has given us another reason to keep up with their wedding style. item.title: How AI Can Expand Opportunities for African Youth – Discussions to Expect at Goalkeepers 2026 Dakar
item.description: AI could be a great equaliser, but only if it’s built intentionally to benefit the people who need it most. Credit: Gates Foundation . During the 2026 ADF-YGL Convening in Lagos , young leaders from across the world, including Africa, gathered at Learn2Earn Academy, an AI talent factory founded by Iyinoluwa Aboyeji . There, the global leaders were introduced to a few students who have been using AI to build solutions for some of the day-to-day challenges that Africans, Nigerians specifically, face. One of them was Anas Masama, who showcased ‘Morrow’, a fintech app that allows offline transfers without internet connectivity. Anas explained that despite the wide coverage of internet providers in Nigeria, the internet’s strength fluctuates or sometimes goes offline and leaves Nigerians stranded at a point of payment. With AI, he built ‘Morrow’ to solve two problems: 1) The embarrassment that a Nigerian might feel due to bad internet connectivity. 2) Time. Anas’ invention is an example of the potential opportunities that exist when Africans leverage AI to solve basic issues. While there are concerns about the risks of AI use in Africa, including hallucinations, stereotypical results and many others, it remains one of the fastest-growing technological advancements in recent times. AI continues to grow and become more efficient, and the most urgent task Africans can embark on is to upskill in how to adopt AI for better use, so the continent doesn’t get left behind. In the 2026 Goalkeepers Report , Bill Gates calls for three actions now that will help AI improve lives and livelihoods for more people in the years ahead: Make AI tools work in every language people speak; ground AI tools in local data; and invest in people and access in the places and populations they are intended to serve. All three suggestions apply to Africa so it can properly leverage AI to expand opportunities. At present, despite how expansive AI has become, it is built in places far away from Africa. This is why Africans, who have access to local data and speak African languages, should build AI tools that incorporate local data and African languages for better use. This way, AI has access to specific data of Africans and will allow it to better understand cultural contexts and pragmatics. This will make a great equaliser rather than make things less equal. Of course, Africans still encounter basic challenges like electricity, connectivity, access to phones, and other issues, but those who have access must maximise it greatly to help others. This year’s Goalkeepers 2026 is centred around this conversation. After hosting engaging and immersive events in the Nordics and New York, Goalkeepers is coming to Dakar on October 29. This event, “Equitable AI and the Future of African Youth”, aims to discuss how AI can create opportunities for Africans across various sectors while also addressing the challenges the continent faces. item.title: Davido, Zlatan & Shoday Turn Their “Nakupenda” Performance Into a London Sing-Along
item.description: Shoday, Zlatan Ibile, and Davido performing Nakupenda live on stage during their London concert setup. Photo Credit: Davido/Instagram “Oh my God, what is this? (What is what?)” You already know what comes next. We’re taking you straight to London, where Davido , Zlatan and Shoday had an entire arena singing along to “ Nakupenda ”. And judging by the crowd, nobody needed convincing to join in. Phones were up, voices were loud, and thousands of fans were enjoying every moment of the performance. There’s something so lovely about watching a song travel from our speakers to a stage thousands of miles away, with a crowd singing every word right back to the artistes. That’s exactly what happened when Davido and Zlatan performed “Nakupenda” alongside Shoday, giving the London audience a performance filled with music, dancing and some very happy fans. Davido took to the stage in a white tank top and green trousers, moving across the platform as the audience sang along. Zlatan joined him in a tactical vest and red trousers, bringing his familiar dance moves into the mix. With dancers adding to the performance and the crowd responding to every verse, there was hardly a moment when the arena wasn’t buzzing. And can we talk about those phone flashlights? Seeing thousands of them raised across the arena while everyone sang together was such a beautiful sight. It’s one thing to enjoy “Nakupenda” through your headphones, but hearing an entire crowd sing it back to Davido, Zlatan and Shoday is a whole different experience. Watch Davido, Zlatan and Shoday perform “Nakupenda” live in London below. item.title: On this day in space! Oct. 24, 1946: V-2 rocket takes 1st photos of Earth from space
item.description: null On October 24, 1946, a V-2 rocket captured the first-ever photo of Earth from space. While these grainy, black-and-white images might not look like much today, they were a huge deal at the time, because no one had ever seen Earth from space before. The V-2 rocket launched from the White Sands Missile Range in New Mexico. It carried a 35-millimeter motion picture camera that captured a new frame every second and a half. The rocket soared to an altitude of about 65 miles before falling back to Earth. Both the rocket and the camera were destroyed after crashing into the Earth at a speed of about 340 miles per hour. But the film survived because it was protected inside a steel case. Scientists had to drive out into the New Mexico desert to retrieve the film. When they saw the images for the first time, the scientists were literally jumping up and down with joy. This photo is the first view of Earth from space taken by a camera on a U.S. Army V-2 rocket launched from White Sands Missile Range in New Mexico on Oct. 24, 1946. (Image credit: U.S. Army) How it mattered The ability to photograph Earth from space drove both an expanded interest to continue pushing into space and led to unexpected societal changes with regards to how humanity considered its home planet. For military and intelligence agencies, the potential now existed for reconnaissance at a far larger scale than what was possible with high-altitude aircraft. That capability expanded to agriculture and meteorological purposes, eventually making Earth observation one of the most common reasons satellites and space stations are deployed into orbit today. Earth photography from space also gave birth to the environmental movement, as people began to see the planet differently. The fragility of this orb became more apparent, as now Earth appeared a "blue marble" set against an endless black void. Want more space history? item.description: Zlatan Ibile and Davita Omoniyi holding hands during their Edo traditional wedding, styled by Goodnews Emmanuel Icon. What a beautiful day for love! Zlatan Ibile and Davita Omoniyi are celebrating their traditional wedding today, and we’re starting the day with their beautiful first look. The Afrobeats star and his bride-to-be have chosen to honour Davita’s Edo heritage with coordinated traditional wedding attire, from her richly embellished burgundy gown to his regal ivory outfit. And there’s so much to love about the details. For their first appearance, Zlatan, whose real name is Omoniyi Temidayo Raphael , and Davita chose to honour her Edo heritage. And what better way to celebrate love than by showing up in outfits that tell a beautiful story about where you come from? Zlatan Ibile kissing Davita Omoniyi’s hand in their custom Edo cultural attire, styled by Goodnews Emmanuel Icon. Davita looked every inch the Edo bride in a custom burgundy gown by Dova Bridals. The corseted mermaid design featured a curved sweetheart neckline, sheer long sleeves and a sweeping side train. Red crystal beads formed beautiful lattice patterns across the gown, while her traditional Okuku braided crown and layers of coral necklaces completed the look. She also carried a black horsehair fly whisk, with a sheer crimson veil draped over her crown. Davita Omoniyi as an Edo bride seated on a carved throne in a custom Dova Bridals gown. And Zlatan? The groom was every bit as regal beside his bride. He wore a custom cream robe by Deji & Kola, topped with a textured ivory coat featuring hand-stitched red beadwork along the shoulders and hem. The red details tied his outfit beautifully to Davita’s, while layers of coral beads, an ivory ceremonial cap and a carved wooden staff completed his traditional look. Zlatan Ibile wearing a custom Deji & Kola cream robe and layered coral beads for his traditional wedding. Styled by Goodnews Emmanuel Icon, the couple posed against a warm ombré backdrop, with Zlatan seated on a carved gold throne beneath a tasseled umbrella. Between the coordinated outfits, the traditional accessories and the beautiful celebration of Davita’s Edo roots, their first wedding look is one we’ll be admiring for a while. item.title: 'Star Trek: Strange New Worlds' was afraid to say anything in season of gimmicks
item.description:
Matthew has more than 30 years of experience talking about movies, TV shows, and video games, and for 20 of those years someone has actually paid him to do it. He's just as surprised as you are.

He has a degree in Film from Vassar College and a degree in gaming from growing up in the '80s and '90s. He has written for both print and online outlets, including The Escapist, MTV, Flixist, Destructoid, Variety, and the Washington Post.

He will still gladly talk anyone's ear off about Marvel, Star Wars, Doctor Who, Zelda, and Star Trek.

It didn’t take long for fans to figure out that the fourth season of "Star Trek: Strange New Worlds" was going to be unlike any season of " Star Trek " before it. The entire season was one giant gimmick, and that gimmick was shoving "Trek" into as many genres as possible and often directly adapting classic films from those genres. You could argue that an entire season of gimmick episodes is a bold risk: putting the characters in fun, wacky situations to see how they react. It could be interesting, but the season we got never made the most of the concept. It was all so safe and paint-by-numbers, and, most importantly, it didn't have anything profound or interesting to say. That should trouble any Trekkie. "Star Trek" — a show built on progressive ideals, thoughtful characters, and boundary-breaking television — was completely and totally afraid to say anything at all. Mash it up, Scotty (Image credit: Paramount) To be clear, "Star Trek" is no stranger to genre mashups, and they're not inherently a bad thing. Trek has been running for nearly 1,000 total episodes, and they've been doing mashups since the very first season of "Star Trek: The Original Series", which featured gangster, historical fiction, and war-themed episodes. The holodeck took things further, giving the writers an excuse to set the action anywhere they could dream up. No more alien planets that look suspiciously like Earth were necessary to completely flip the series’ genre; just work up a hologram malfunction and suddenly "Trek" is a Sherlock Holmes-esque mystery or a noir thriller. And even without the holodeck, genres are fluid things that often take from each other to tell stories within each other’s realms. But while "Trek" has always dabbled, it's never done an entire season of genre episodes… in fact, that might be unprecedented in all of science fiction TV itself, let alone "Star Trek". This season of "SNW" didn’t use occasional gimmicks to take a break from space fare; it was all gimmick, all the time. Check out the episode rundown below: Episode 1: Dinosaur adventure/western (Land of the Lost) Episode 2: Space horror (Event Horizon) Episode 3: Raunchy comedy (The Hangover) Episode 4: Wartime drama (Casablanca)* Episode 5: Puppets (The Muppets) Episode 6: Disaster movie/real-time story (The Poseidon Adventure) Episode 7: Soap opera (Days of Our Lives) Episode 8: Cold War film/submarine movie (The Hunt for Red October) Episod

item.title: Medusa's eye, Halloween fireballs and more: 5 skywatching targets to look out for this spooky season
item.description: null The spooky season is officially here! To celebrate, we've put together a list of five Halloween-themed skywatching targets that you can enjoy with nothing but the naked eye or binoculars and, of course, clear skies. Over millennia, the night sky has helped shape human beliefs. In return, we have imprinted our myths, stories and perceptions upon it, seeing monsters and mythology in the twinkling lights of the stars and assigning sinister aspects to innocent cosmic objects. Many of these ghostly impressions and meanings have survived to the present day. Here are a few of our favorites. The Pleiades open star cluster Don't be fooled by their beauty; the blue-white stars of the Pleiades are dripping in spooky lore. Ancient Celtic druids would hold the celebration of Samhain — the precursor to Halloween — when the star cluster reached its highest point in the autumn night sky at midnight . The Pleiades open star cluster glows in the blackness of space. (Image credit: Photo by Lorenzo Di Cola/NurPhoto via Getty Images) The veil separating the worlds of the living and the dead was believed to be at its thinnest around this time, granting the departed a brief window to visit the living before the realms separated once again. The Pleiades appears as a tight collection of six or seven bright twinkling stars to the naked eye, while a pair of binoculars will reveal dozens more of the 1,000-strong star cluster. How to find the Pleiades in October using Orion's Belt. (Image credit: Created by Anthony Wood in Canva.) Stargazers in the U.S. can find the Pleiades using the three familiar stars of Orion's Belt , which glisten in the eastern sky in the hours preceding midnight. Trace an imaginary line upward through the trio of stars until you find the bright orange star Aldebaran, which represents an eye of the great bull represented in the constellation Taurus . The Pleiades can be found glowing less than 15 degrees above! (Reminder: Your clenched fist held at arm's length covers about 10 degrees of sky.) The 'Demon Star' Algol Next we turn our gaze to the "Demon Star" Algol — a beautiful binary system that represents an eye of the monstrous Gorgon Medusa, whose severed head is depicted in the constellation Perseus . The demon star Algol shines above the southeastern horizon after sunset in October. (Image credit: Created by Anthony Wood in Canva.) The demonic eye appears to "wink" at us every 2.867 days, as one of a pair of co-orbiting stars eclipses the other, making Algol appear 3.3 times dimmer than usual at the climax, or "minima," of each 10-hour eclipse. Algol won't be eclipsed on Halloween night in 2026, though you may notice its light dim during the surrounding minima on Oct. 29 and Nov. 1, according to Sky and Telescope . Cetus, the sea monster The night sky is often described as a sea of stars, so it's only fitting that a monster lurks within its depths. item.title: SpaceX launches Starlink satellites from California as Falcon 9 cadence slows (video)
item.description: null SpaceX launched its newest batch of Starlink broadband internet satellites today (Oct. 23) from the California coast. The spacecraft, Starlink Group 15-15, were stacked 27 high inside the payload fairing of a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket , which lifted off from Pad 4E at Vandenberg Space Force Base at 6:48 p.m. EDT (2248 GMT; 3:48 p.m. local time in California). The rocket's first stage booster, designated B1063, executed its main engine cutoff and stage separation about 2.5 minutes into flight, sending the second stage to continue onward to low Earth orbit (LEO). The vehicle's two-piece protective payload fairing was jettisoned just before T+3 minutes. A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket launches 27 Starlink satellites from California on Oct. 23, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) The booster, meanwhile, reoriented for its descent back to Earth. As the mission clock passed 8 minutes, B1063 began its landing burn, and it touched down about 20 seconds later on SpaceX's droneship "Of Course I Still Love You." This was the 36th launch and landing for B1063, which notably launched NASA's DART asteroid-smashing mission in November 2021. The Falcon 9's upper stage completed its first engine burn shortly after B1063 landed and will coast for about 45 minutes before initiating a second and final orbital insertion burn. Following that burn's execution, deployment of the vehicle's 27 satellites into LEO is scheduled to begin 62 minutes after launch. The Falcon 9's first stage, shortly after its drone-ship landing on Oct. 23, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) Previous Booster B1063 launches Sentinel-6 Michael Freilich | DART | Transporter-7 | Iridium OneWeb | SDA-0B | NROL-113 | NROL-167 | NROL-149 | NAOS | 26 Starlink missions Today's Starlink liftoff adds to SpaceX's growing constellation of more than 11,000 active spacecraft. But Starlinks aren't launching quite as often as they used to, as SpaceX shifts its focus from the Falcon 9 to its bigger and more powerful Starship rocket. Starship is designed for full reusability and is equipped with a payload bay outfitted to accommodate SpaceX's upgraded Version 3 Starlink satellites, which are too large for the workhorse Falcon 9. Starship is still under development, but once the rocket begins operational flights (and that day is getting closer), SpaceX plans to phase out the Falcon 9 and its Falcon Heavy variant almost entirely. Falcon 9's 100th launch of 2026 was the Starlink 10-49 group from SpaceX's pad at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, which was later revealed to be the final Falcon 9 Starlink mission that would fly from Florida's Space Coast. The same might soon be true for Starlink launches from the West Coast as well. The reduction in missions lifting off from Florida has slowed Falcon 9's Starlink launch cadence considerably. At their peak, these missions were flying every two to three days. But the most recent one before today lifted off 11 days ago , and that launch itself was the first Starlink mission in more than

item.title: NASA lays out plan for Artemis 3 moon-lander test flight —but when will it launch?
item.description: null NASA just gave us our best look yet at its Artemis III moon-lander test flight. The agency laid out a detailed concept of operations for Artemis III today (Oct. 23) during a press conference at Kennedy Space Center , stressing how important the flight is to its moon plans and how challenging it will be to make everything go right. "We're launching three of the most powerful rockets in the world, and undertaking what is likely the most complicated launch campaign ever undertaken," Jeremy Parsons, NASA’s Artemis program manager, said during today's event, which lasted more than two hours. The baseline concept of operations for NASA's Artemis III docking test in low Earth orbit. (Image credit: NASA) Those three rockets are NASA's Space Launch System (SLS), SpaceX's Starship and Blue Origin's New Glenn , all of which will fly from Florida's Space Coast. If all goes according to plan, New Glenn will lift off first, carrying Blue Origin's Blue Moon lunar lander to low Earth orbit (LEO). SLS will go next, launching the Artemis III astronauts — NASA's Randy Bresnik, Andre Douglas and Frank Rubio, and the European Space Agency's Luca Parmitano — aboard NASA's Orion spacecraft . SLS will deploy Orion into a highly elliptical orbit, one that gets as close to Earth as 18 miles (29 kilometers) and as far away as 1,122 miles (1,806 km), according to Parsons. The capsule will then maneuver itself into an orbit with an altitude of about 345 miles (555 km). "That's really about getting thermal stability," Parsons said. "Orion was built as a deep-space vehicle, and so we're going to have to really manage the thermal environments, which are higher in a low Earth orbit." The Artemis III crew will spend two days checking out Orion and its systems in LEO before meeting up with Blue Moon, which will take place on Flight Day 3 at an altitude of 273 miles (439 km). "Over the next two days, the crew will conduct operations docked with Blue Moon," Parsons said. "They're going to open up the hatch. They're going to enter the lander. They're going to evaluate the environmental controls, the life support systems. We'll confirm that the spacecraft can maintain the right atmospheric pressure, and we're also going to test emergency scenarios, dual vehicle control, and we're going to put our Mission Control teams through their paces." After those operations are complete — likely on Flight Day 6 or thereabouts — Starship will launch, with a specially built docking adapter on its nose. The SpaceX vehicle — the 171-foot-tall (52 meters) upper stage of its fully reusable Starship megarocket — will meet up with Orion in LEO on Flight Day 8, at an altitude of about 237 miles (381 km). But this will be a very different encounter than the rendezvous with Blue Moon. "The demonstration with Starship is shorter, about two hours," Parsons said. "The crew will not enter the Starship during the mission, but it gives us critical data and allows us to really understand the forces of docking

item.title: On this day in space! Oct. 23, 2007: NASA launches Harmony module to ISS on STS-120 space shuttle mission
item.description: null On October 23, 2007, the space shuttle Discovery launched the Harmony module to the International Space Station . The Harmony module is a utility hub 14 feet wide and 24 feet long, or about the length of a minibus. It joins the European Space Agency's Columbus module and Japan's Kibo laboratory and serves as the crew quarters for the American astronauts. Once it was installed, the space station grew from about the size of a three-bedroom house to something more like a five-bedroom house. When astronauts delivered Harmony to the space station , they left it temporarily attached to the Unity node. After the shuttle left, astronauts used the space station's robotic arm to move the shuttle docking port out of the way at the Destiny module. This made room for Harmony to then dock at its permanent home next to the Destiny module. The U.S. Harmony node flew to space aboard space shuttle Discovery during mission STS-120, in October 2007, to be a connecting module and allow a larger space station. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered In 2007, the International Space Station was much smaller than it is today in terms of living space for its astronaut crew. The Harmony connecting module changed all that. The STS-120 mission opened a new phase of ISS expansion by adding a vital connecting hub for future modules. Prior to Harmony's launch, the last new room addition to the ISS had occurred in 2001, when Russia's Pirs docking module (since discarded) arrived. The Harmony module ( its original name was Node 2 ), was the second NASA-led hub module (after the Unity, or Node 1, module) for the ISS. It was built for NASA by the Italy-based Thales Alenia Space and is covered with five "common berthing mechanisms," or connecting points for different ISS modules. After the two-week STS-120 flight, Harmony was moved from a temporary berth at the Unity module to the forward port on the NASA's main Destiny laboratory. Once there, it served as a connection point for Europe's Columbus lab on the starboard side, and Japan's massive Kibo lab on the port side. Some of its ports have been used by visiting caargo ships and a docking port on its roof allows visiting vehicles to park there. Inside the module are eight payload racks that include four used for avionics and four others for either stowage or crew quarters. NASA's astronaut crew quarters are based in the Harmony module. The name Harmony was selected durng a public naming contest by NASA. Want more space history? item.title: Halley's Comet dazzles from afar in spectacular astrophoto of Orionid meteor shower
item.description: null Tim McCollum captured a stunning view of Orionid meteors in the early hours of Oct. 21. (Image credit: Tim McCollum) Astrophotographer Tim McCollum captured a spectacular view of Orionid meteors sharing the night sky with a host of deep sky wonders on Oct. 21, as the annual shooting star display ramped up to peak activity. Comet 1P/Halley may be over 3 billion miles (4.8 kilometers) from Earth , but that didn't stop it from putting on a breathtaking display earlier this week, as particles cast off by the ancient wanderer carved a fiery path through the autumn sky. McCollum was able to capture a trio of vivid Orionid meteors as they streaked through the night sky above the city of Toccoa, Georgia, between 3-4 a.m. on Oct. 21. Each of the shooting stars can be seen racing away from the shower's apparent point of origin — or radiant — which is located close to the red giant star Betelgeuse in the constellation Orion . Successfully imaging a shooting star takes a combination of skill, luck and patience. McCollum photographed the meteors over the course of multiple 30-second exposures taken with a Canon EOS Ra camera and RF 28-70 f2.0 lens, which was fixed unerringly on the radiant with the aid of a star tracker. The individual exposures were then combined into a single composite image using the astrophoto software PixInsight. Nebulas and star clusters shine alongside fast-moving Orionid meteors. (Image credit: Tim McCollum) Canon EOS R7 camera (Image credit: Future/Kimberley Lane) The Canon EOS R7 is the best camera for beginners. Despite its crop sensor, the EOS R7 can rival most full-frame cameras. It features a 34.4MP sensor, ISO range up to 32,000 and a video capability of 4K UHD 60p. It has the best tools to help a beginner master photography. Read our full Canon EOS R7 review. The familiar stars of Orion's Belt glisten to the right of McCollum's image, close to the glow of the Orion Nebula — one of the nearest major star forming regions to Earth. The Rosette Nebula (Caldwell 49) can also be spotted embedded in the dense starfield and dust lanes of the Milky Way's galactic plane, which runs diagonally through the composite image, as can numerous star clusters. The Orionid meteor shower is active until Nov. 7, so be sure to head outside over the next few nights for a chance to spot one of Comet 1P/Halley's dazzling shooting stars . If you're lucky, you may even spot a Halloween Fireball belonging to the Taurid meteor shower , as Earth passes through the debris streams cast off by Comet 2P/Encke! Why not read our handy guide to photographing shooting stars ? You can also take a look at our picks of the best lenses and cameras for astrophotography available in 2026, including the Canon EOS R8 , which delivers the essential interval shooting functionality you need to capture meteors without bursting the bank. item.description: The Forum of Women in Film and Television Nigeria (FWIFT) will host its upcoming national convention on Thursday, October 29, 2026, at the historic Glover Memorial Hall in Lagos. Running from 11:00 AM to 4:00 PM, the event centers on the theme “ One Industry, Many Voices: We Build Together. “ The gathering will unite women across film, television, radio, advertising, and digital media to connect, share insights, and create agency for one another across sectors. Art cultural expert and curator Mrs. Sandra Mbanefo Obiago will deliver the keynote address. The program features interactive panel discussions, break-out sessions, speed networking, and a fireside chat titled “The Cross Over: A Career Beyond Borders.” Featured speakers and panellists joining the conversation include media executive Kadaria Ahmed, filmmaker Biodun Stephens, media personality Gbemi Olateru-Olagbegi, executive director Rosemary Egabor-Afolahan, and Esosa Osagiede. Register Here . “Our goal is to build an interconnected media ecosystem where women across screen, broadcast, and digital platforms can pool resources and create collective momentum,” said FWIFT leadership . “By bringing together diverse practitioners under one roof, we are establishing practical pathways for cross-industry growth, mentorship, and cross-border careers that elevate African storytelling on the global stage. “ Event Details: Event : FWIFT Annual Convention 2026 Theme : One Industry, Many Voices: We Build Together Date : Thursday, October 29, 2026 Time : 11:00 AM – 4:00 PM WAT Venue : The Glover Memorial Hall, 4 Customs Street, Lagos Keynote Speaker : Sandra Mbanefo Obiago Featured Speakers : Kadaria Ahmed, Biodun Stephens, Gbemi Olateru-Olagbegi, Rosemary Egabor-Afolahan, Esosa Osagiede Admission : Free (Compulsory Online Registration) Registration lin k: https://forms.gle/qSp31foLEHvHQckMA Sponsor : African Women’s Development Fund: The convention is supported by the African Women’s Development Fund (AWDF) About FWIFT Nigeria The Forum of Women in Film and Television Nigeria (FWIFT) is a professional organization dedicated to empowering Nigerian women in screen-based, audio, and digital media through advocacy, skill acquisition, mentorship, and strategic networking. item.title: Never finishing the fight: Where did Xbox go wrong with Halo?
item.description: Halo: Campaign Evolved was Xbox’s second attempt at refreshing the 2001 sci-fi FPS classic, and it is perfectly fine. A cromulent remake, if ever there was one, but it’s hardly a franchise-saver, especially as Xbox looks to rethink its studio structure and approach to renowned IPs like Halo or Gears of War . Halo hasn’t been the same since original developer Bungie — now owned by Sony and working on Destiny and Marathon — departed, leaving 343 Industries (now Halo Studios) to guide the franchise. Neither Halo 4 nor 5 meaningfully evolved the gameplay formula or overarching narrative. Halo Infinite found more success by reheating what “old Halo felt like” and sticking it into a half-baked open world, but it still felt far from the series’ glory days. This year’s full remake of Combat Evolved's campaign delivered exactly what it promised: a shiny, 2026 version of the game that made audiences fall in love with the franchise. It was a clear attempt to reignite faith in 343’s vision, but how is a faithful, shinier remake proof of anything? It might not even matter anymore, as the new Xbox leadership has rocked the ship again, leaving Master Chief and the universe’s future cloudier than ever before. Now, with rumors of a reboot being considered at new steward Activision, is there hope for the Spartans, or will Xbox run into another dead end? Rebooted or not, Halo needs to leave Master Chief behind (Image credit: Xbox Game Studios) It looks like the ‘Halo Studios’ moniker only lasted a single (remade) game, as Xbox has recently announced that Call of Duty maker and publisher Activision — which houses many FPS-oriented studios — is taking over development, essentially leaving the 343 veterans as a minor support studio, which translates into more layoffs . If we put aside the human and institutional cost of this whole back-and-forth over the years (a big ask in today’s climate), there are reasons to be optimistic about the quality of an Activision-developed Halo. Regardless of what you think about the Call of Duty IP in 2026 and the publisher’s overall vision for it, it’s clear there’s plenty of talent holding everything together and, more importantly, enough experience to iterate on what Halo’s multiplayer side needs to shine bright again. (Image credit: Xbox Game Studios) But this won’t fix the larger issue with Halo, which is that Master Chief should’ve been left behind long ago. Like it or not, it’s difficult to deny Halo’s “golden era” ended with Halo: Reach (Bungie’s swansong under Xbox) and the Halo Wars spinoffs, which took the series into the real-time strategy genre. These games were wildly different, but they had one core thing in common: they made the sci-fi setting feel bigger instead of smaller, offering the perfect blueprint to build upon in a post-Halo 3 world. There’s nothing inherently wrong with the Master Chief. Franchises can be built around iconic characters like Mario or Lara Croft. But in the post-Bungie era, his role c

item.title: Malaria Parasite Caught in the Act of Breaking and Entering
item.description: In medieval Italy, it was accepted wisdom that anyone walking near a swamp risked falling ill from “bad air” — mala aria. Victims were struck with fever, headache, nausea, and chills, and occasionally the illness escalated to vomiting, jaundice, and death. Today, we still call this affliction malaria. For much of human history, it has ravaged populations in humid tropical and subtropical regions… Source

item.title: A farewell to BioWare, maker of some of the best games of the 21st century | Lucy James
item.description: The closure of the studio responsible for some of the best games of the 21st century leaves the world of RPGs feeling smaller without the hope of another instalment of the much-loved sci-fi series Earlier this week, EA announced the closure of BioWare, a game studio with a 30-year history of compelling role-playing games, complex characters and bold, choice-driven narratives. Its forthcoming game in the Mass Effect sci-fi series has been cancelled, and more than 400 people are losing their jobs. As someone who has worked in the video games industry for 15 years and spent almost 20 as a BioWare fan, I am among millions of mourners today. It’s not terribly hard to see why BioWare got the chop. Its parent company has been saddled with $20bn of debt thanks to a recent leveraged buyout involving Jared Kushner and the Saudi wealth fund. EA was looking for weight to cut loose, and despite its hardcore fanbase and reputation for genre-defining RPGs such as Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic and Dragon Age, BioWare hadn’t put out a critical or commercial hit in over 10 years. Its forthcoming game, titled Mass Effect: Universe according to a leaked trailer , was announced back in 2020. Despite some flashy teases, it was still years away from release. Continue reading...

item.title: Private Griffin moon lander gets put to the test | Space photo of the day for Oct. 23, 2026
item.description: null The Griffin-1 lunar lander undergoes testing at NASA's Jet Propulsion Lab. (Image credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech) The robotic Griffin lunar lander has passed a host of critical tests ahead of its first-ever moon mission, which is scheduled to launch later this year. What is it? At NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) in Southern California, Voyager Technologies' Griffin Mission One (or Griffin-1 ) lunar lander has gone through an absolute gauntlet of tests. The spacecraft was put through environmental testing that explored how the vehicle will fare in the extreme conditions it will experience on its ride to the surface of the moon . This testing simulated the extreme temperatures, shaking and even the sounds that the spacecraft will experience from launch to landing. And, as JPL announced recently, the lander passed this series of tests with flying colors, as we can see in this image snapped Aug. 31 of the lander inside the 25-foot-wide (7.6 meters) space simulator at JPL. "NASA JPL’s Environmental Test Laboratory has been putting robotic explorers to the test since the Ranger program gave us NASA’s first up-close views of the moon's surface in the mid-1960s. We’re proud to provide our expertise and facilities to support this new phase of commercial lunar exploration," Charles Whetsel, manager for the Exploration Systems Development Office at JPL, said in a statement . Why is it incredible? Griffin-1 is expected to launch to the moon later this year as part of NASA's CLPS (Commercial Lunar Payload Services) initiative. The spacecraft will carry over 1,100 pounds (455 kilograms) of cargo to its landing site near the lunar south pole. In this cargo will be science experiments and new technologies that will be tested on the moon's surface, including Astrolab's FLIP rover , which will explore the lunar surface with a history-making supercomputer onboard. This suite of experimental hardware won't just expand our understanding of the moon up close. Griffin-1's exploration will also help set the stage for a future, crewed moon base , which NASA aims to build near the south pole over the next half-decade or so.

item.title: Yemi Alade Is Counting Cash and Serving Looks in “Alhaja” Video
item.description: Yemi Alade wears a gold-embroidered black abaya in her “Alhaja” music video. We love how Yemi Alade gives us something new to talk about with each music video. If she isn’t channelling a photographer who could give Don Jazzy a run for his money, she’s stepping into the shoes of an Alhaja who clearly has money to spend, and she’s having a great time doing it. In the official music video for “Alhaja”, a standout track from her latest album, It’s Yemi Alade , the Afropop star leans into rich cultural aesthetics, striking outfits and scenes that feel like a celebration of success. Directed by Clarence Peters , the video plays with neon lighting, atmospheric torchlight and a cast that knows how to make an entrance. Yemi Alade holds a stack of cash in a scene from her “Alhaja” music video. Yemi has a wardrobe change for every mood, too. In one scene, she appears in a traditional red outfit, complete with a structured headwrap and layers of coral beads. Then comes a black-and-gold embroidered abaya, paired with bold gold hand jewellery and ornate rings. She’s giving us an Alhaja who knows exactly what she’s worth, and the styling makes sure we don’t miss it. Yemi Alade holds a stack of cash in a scene from her “Alhaja” music video. The details around her are just as fun. Vintage cars set the scene, traditional drums bring in the cultural touches, and cast members count cash beneath warm lanterns. It all adds to the video’s celebration of identity, prosperity and personal achievement, with Yemi right at the centre of it. With “Alhaja”, Yemi Alade gives us another music video with a distinct visual world, memorable styling and plenty of personality. And really, would we expect anything less? item.title: What is The Hidden Cost of Nigerian Women’s Unpaid Labour?
item.description: Mother and children preparing food in a bright, cosy kitchen setting. Credit: RDNE Stock Project/Pexels. Fadekemi was six when she first felt the sting of splattered hot oil on her skin. She recalls her mother’s stern voice instructing her on how to make stew the way her father liked it. Fifty-one years and thousands of stew pots later, Fadekemi still wonders if that’s all she was made to do. In different parts of Nigeria today, there are millions of women like Fadekemi, each spending at least 5 hours daily on unpaid care and domestic work. Although Nigerians rarely pay women for care and domestic duties, research shows that it is real work with an annual economic value of up to $111 billion . How Women Carry Nigeria’s Unpaid Labour According to the Nigeria Time Use Survey (NTUS) 2024 report, the average Nigerian woman spends 21% of her day on unpaid domestic and care work ; this equals 5 extra hours, while men spend just one hour on unpaid work. This means that after spending 8 hours at work, she spends another 5 hours doing childcare and household work, making it a double shift. Yet when you look at the economic drivers of Nigeria’s economy, her time or work does not count; it is seen as a woman’s work. This inequality is seen as invisible labour. We see it show up in different phases of women’s lives, yet we still miss how heavy an unequal burden this is. Right from when a girl is 13, she becomes an unpaid labourer, doing domestic chores, taking care of siblings, yet these contributions are seen as nothing to Nigeria’s GDP. For Fadekemi, this unpaid labour started at six, continued into her teenage years, where she became a caregiver for her siblings, extended into motherhood, and now, as a grandmother, she continues to be a caregiver for her grandchildren because even traditions like Omugwo exclude men from care duties. Behind those hours of unpaid labour is a missed opportunity for the country’s GDP growth. What Happens When Care Is Shared? In a 2026 study published in BMC Paediatrics, over 64% of women said they were the primary caregivers of their newborn children. In some cases, this is a result of traditional belief systems that reinforce gender roles and assign domestic duties to women. In other cases, it is a systemic failure caused by policies that reinforce gender inequality. In Nigeria, for example, mothers are entitled to maternity leave with 50% pay, while only fathers in the civil service are entitled to 14 days of paternity leave. So what happens to private sector fathers? The national policy designs them to be absent fathers from day one and reinforces the narrative that their sole role is to be a provider and presence doesn’t matter. Experts have highlighted that cutting a new mother’s salary by 50% while excluding most fathers from paid leave reinforces the belief that a man’s primary duty is to be a financial provider and makes it harder for them to be present. And when that happens, care once again becomes the woman’s job.

item.title: 25 and Golden! Dede Ashiogwu Celebrates in a Gorgeous Butter-Yellow Two-Piece
item.description: Dede celebrates her 25th birthday in a draped butter yellow chiffon set. Butter yellow on melanin is already a winning combination, but Big Brother Naija Season 10 star Dede is taking it somewhere much more fabulous. Celebrating her birthday on 23 October 2026, the content creator, whose full name is Ashiogwu Precious , has gifted us a set of Renaissance-inspired portraits that could easily pass for paintings in a grand old gallery. And the outfit at the centre of it all? A custom butter-yellow two-piece that makes a very good case for giving this pretty shade a spot in your wardrobe. Dede wears a custom butter yellow gathering bandeau top and low-rise train skirt by Precious Phillips. Dede handled the creative direction herself, working with designer Precious Phillips on a gathered bandeau top and a low-rise maxi skirt that follows her figure before spilling into a floor-sweeping train. The colour is gorgeous against her skin, and that dramatic silhouette gives the look a regal, almost otherworldly quality without feeling stuck in another century. Of course, the beauty look had to keep up. Yellow feathers frame her eyes, a thick side-braided ponytail sweeps through her hair, and her glowing makeup ties everything together. Add a golden hand mirror and a moody, canvas-style backdrop, and you have birthday portraits that look as though they were dreamed up in an artist’s studio. Dede poses with a golden handheld mirror in her self-styled Renaissance birthday shoot. The best part is that you don’t need a Renaissance-inspired photoshoot to take a little inspiration from Dede. Butter yellow works beautifully in flowing chiffon, sheer mesh and other lightweight fabrics, whether you’re dressing for a birthday dinner or simply want to try something new. Gold jewellery complements the shade beautifully, while pared-back accessories give statement silhouettes and playful eye makeup room to shine. Dede complements her birthday look with soft yellow feather eye flourishes and gold leaf drop earrings. Dede may have given butter yellow the full birthday-treatment treatment, but the takeaway is simple: this shade deserves a place in your fashion rotation. Ashiogwu Precious (Dede) marks her 25th birthday in a butter yellow two-piece set by Precious Phillips. Ashiogwu Precious (Dede) seated beside warm floral accents in her custom Precious Phillips birthday outfit. *** Photo Credit: Ashiogwu Precious/Instagram The post 25 and Golden! item.title: Janelle Monáe Spreads Her Fashion Wings in a Sculptural Robert Wun Gown
item.description: Janelle Monáe wears a custom blue sequined Robert Wun gown at the 2026 Academy Museum Gala. Butterfly in a dress? Janelle Monáe says bring it on! We’ve seen butterflies inspire jewellery, hair accessories and even prints on dresses, but a giant, three-dimensional butterfly forming the bodice of a gown? Now that’s something worth talking about. And who better to wear it than the acclaimed singer, songwriter, and actress Janelle Monáe, who has never been afraid to have a little fun with fashion? For the 6th Annual Academy Museum Gala, held on 17 October 2026 in Los Angeles, the singer and actress known for her memorable roles in Hidden Figures , Moonlight , and Glass Onion , stepped onto the red carpet in a Robert Wun creation that looked like a butterfly had spread its wings right across her chest. The gown, from the designer’s Fall 2026 Couture collection, featured a fitted mermaid silhouette covered in sequins that moved from rich blue to black. But the real attraction was that enormous three-dimensional butterfly bodice, with its wings extending across her upper body. Janelle Monáe attends the 2026 Academy Museum Gala in a custom Robert Wun mermaid dress. And Janelle wasn’t about to let the butterfly theme end with the dress. Styled by Alexandra Mandelkorn , she paired the gown with sheer opera-length gloves, metallic blue stiletto nails and a soft pixie cut finished with a little butterfly hair clip. Even the smallest details played along with the look, without competing with that spectacular bodice. Janelle Monáe in custom Robert Wun Couture at the 6th Annual Academy Museum Gala. Now, if you’re wondering how to borrow a little inspiration from this look without wearing an enormous butterfly to your next event, there’s something to learn from Janelle’s styling. When your outfit already has a striking feature, you can afford to keep everything else simple. Skip the heavy necklaces, let the shape of the dress do its thing and choose accessories that complement its colours. And those shades of blue are worth experimenting with, too. Cobalt, navy and other rich jewel tones can look beautiful together, especially when you carry a little of the colour into your makeup or accessories. Janelle’s look might be straight from the couture runway, but the styling ideas are ones you can have fun with in your own wardrobe. Janelle Monáe showcases the three-dimensional butterfly bodice of her Robert Wun Fall 2026 Couture gown. Janelle Monáe wearing blue eye makeup and metallic nails to match her Robert Wun butterfly gown. *** Photo Credit: Janelle Monáe/Instagram The post Janelle Monáe Spreads Her Fashion Wings in a Sculptural Robert Wun Gown appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. item.title: Is a job guarantee the solution to mass AI unemployment?
item.description: An old idea springs anew as a chorus of influential voices predicts that AI may trigger crises of vast magnitude In a preface to his book Capitalism and Freedom, the American economist Milton Friedman famously observed that a crisis can propel once-fringe ideas into the political mainstream. “Only a crisis – actual or perceived – produces real change. When that crisis occurs, the actions that are taken depend on the ideas that are lying around,” he wrote. The job of intellectuals, thinktanks and economists, he argued, is to refine the quality of these ambient ideas, so that good ones are ready when disaster strikes. Continue reading...

item.title: Adekunle Gold Foundation and PESA Launch ‘We Are Not Done’ Sickle Cell Impact Initiative
item.description: The Adekunle Gold Foundation (AG Foundation), in partnership with Pesa , has launched We’re Not Done: AG Foundation Sickle Cell Impact Initiative , a new programme designed to strengthen organisations providing critical support to people living with sickle cell disease. Launching with a $20,000 commitment from Pesa , the initiative will provide funding to selected sickle cell organisations, helping them expand their work across healthcare access, patient support, education, awareness and advocacy. For its inaugural cycle, We’re Not Done will support AG Foundation’s work alongside the following 4 beneficiaries, Sickle Cell Advocacy Management Initiative (NIGERIA), Not Just You (CANADA), Sickle Life (GHANA), It Takes A Village (UK) recognizing the important work each organisation is already doing within the sickle cell community. The funding will enable the organisations to strengthen existing programmes, expand their reach and deepen their impact. For A dekunle Gold, who has lived openly with sickle cell disease and used his platform to advocate for the community, We’re Not Done represents a commitment to supporting the organisations already doing vital work on the ground. “ We’re Not Done is about turning awareness into action. There are incredible organisations working every day to improve the lives of people living with sickle cell, and together with Pesa, we want to give them more resources to do that work and reach even more people.” Adekunle Gold said. Pesa joins the initiative as its programme partner , supporting both the launch and first cycle of impact. “ Sickle cell affects many people in the Nigerian and wider Black communities we serve. These are our friends, colleagues, and loved ones. Adekunle Gold has shown how a personal connection to an issue can become a force for meaningful change, and we’re proud to support the launch of We’re Not Done , an initiative dedicated to raising awareness and supporting the sickle cell community. Through our partnership with the AG Foundation and the other participating foundations, we hope to go beyond awareness and contribute to meaningful, tangible support for individuals and families affected by sickle cell, ” said Tosin Olaniyi (Head, Global Growth & Marketing, Pesa) Through We’re Not Done , AG Foundation, with the support of Pesa, aims to build a platform that combines funding, advocacy and visibility to strengthen the wider sickle cell ecosystem and create measurable, lasting impact. Because for the sickle cell community, we’re not done. About Adekunle Gold Foundation Adekunle Gold Foundation was founded in 2023 by singer/songwriter Adekunle Gold. The foundation is committed to improving the lives of those living with sickle cell disease through healthcare access, advocacy, and awareness. item.title: Macro Photographer, Dara Ojo, Shares Stories Behind Some of His Photographs
item.description: Following our feature on Dara Ojo , a Nigerian macro photographer on his journey into photography and his forthcoming book, we invited him to share stories behind three of his selected photographs. Dara grew up in Nigeria and is currently based in Canada, but his photography journey began in China during the COVID-19 pandemic. You can read Dara’s story here while reading the stories behind his selected photographs. Hello Dara, we hope you’re well. Thank you for sharing your journey with us. You have selected three photographs to tell us the stories behind. Why these photos? Thank you for having me. The photos I selected are Planthopper Nymph, Silkworm Moth and Leafhopper Infected by Metarhizium Fungus. I selected them because they all have something in common: Costa Rica. They were all shot in Costa Rica. Let me share the story behind each, and you will get a proper picture. Silkworm Moth Silkworm Moth by Nigerian macro photographer Dara Ojo. I photographed this beautiful silkworm moth in Costa Rica while filming the PBS documentary Bugs That Rule the World . What I love about moths is how often people underestimate them. Many assume they’re dull, but when you get close enough, you discover incredible colours, patterns and textures. This particular moth was a wonderful example of that hidden beauty. Being able to document creatures like this while working on a wildlife documentary was a special experience, and it’s a reminder of how much of nature’s beauty we overlook simply because we don’t stop to look closely. Leafhopper Infected by Metarhizium Fungus Leafhopper overtaken by Fungi. Photo by Dara Ojo. This is probably one of the strangest things I’ve photographed in nature. I came across this leafhopper in Costa Rica, and a parasitic fungus called Metarhizium had completely overtaken its body . The fungus infects insects, grows inside their bodies and eventually kills them. Under suitable conditions, it then grows out of the insect’s body and produces spores that can infect other insects. It’s fascinating and a little unsettling. If you’ve watched The Last of Us , you’ll probably recognise the inspiration behind the show’s fictional fungal infection, although the fungi involved are different. What makes this photograph so remarkable to me is that it almost looks like something from a science fiction movie, yet it’s a real interaction happening in nature. Sometimes, the natural world is far stranger than anything we could imagine. Planthopper Nymph Planthopper nymph by Nigerian macro photographer Dara Ojo. This is one of the trickiest little creatures I’ve ever photographed. It’s a planthopper nymph, a tiny insect with beautiful, waxy strands extending from the back of its body. Finding one is difficult enough because they’re incredibly small, but getting a good photograph is another challenge entirely. They have a habit of turning away whenever you try to photograph them, almost as though they’re deliberately avoiding the camera. You have to be

item.title: Veteran Nollywood Actor Francis Duru Passes Away at 57 | Read Family Statement
item.description: Veteran Nollywood actor Francis Duru has passed away at the age of 57. Photo Credit: Francis Duru/Instagram The Nigerian film industry has been thrown into mourning following the sad passing of veteran Nollywood actor, director,and academic, Francis Duru . The respected movie star passed away at the age of 57 following a brief illness, leaving behind a incredible legacy that spans over three decades of memorable performances across television and cinema. Sharing the heartbreaking news with fans and well-wishers on his official Instagram page, his family released a moving statement: We, the family of Francis Duru, regret to announce his passing following a brief illness. We appreciate your prayers, love, and understanding. May his soul rest in perfect peace. Amen. A true pioneer of modern Nollywood, Francis Duru made his screen debut back in 1989 in the feature Missing Mark , before shooting to nationwide fame for his unforgettable portrayal of Ahanna in Amaka Igwe ’s 1995 classic Rattlesnake . Over the years, he cemented his status as a household name with stellar roles in acclaimed movies such as Blood Money , Mama Sunday , Total Control , Home in Exile , Mboputa , and Stigma . Beyond his stellar career in front of the camera, Duru was a dedicated academic holding a degree in Theatre Arts from the University of Port Harcourt, and a passionate advocate who served as a United Nations Ambassador of Peace and as interim President of the Actors Guild of Nigeria (AGN). Francis Duru is survived by his loving wife, Adokiye Duru , whom he married in 2003, and their children The post Veteran Nollywood Actor Francis Duru Passes Away at 57 | Read Family Statement appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. item.title: Naomi Ackie Was Anything but Basic in Sculptural Schiaparelli at Paris Fashion Week
item.description: Naomi Ackie Naomi Ackie has been delivering some serious fashion moments lately, and her appearance at the Schiaparelli show during Paris Fashion Week is another one for the books. The British-Grenadian actress wore a striking black, single-sleeved gown that perfectly captured the house’s surrealist sensibility. Thousands of finely worked pleats created an almost liquid effect, hugging her figure before falling into a dramatic thigh-high slit. But what really makes this look special is the exaggerated sleeve, which gives the otherwise sleek silhouette an architectural quality. Naomi has worn the brand a few times, and we love how she always embraces the brand’s aesthetic without letting it overwhelm her. The sculptural statement earrings and signature face-motif clutch brought just the right amount of the house’s eccentricity, while her slicked-back ponytail kept the overall look sharp and modern. item.description: Reigning African beauty queens Jihan Mohin Dimack, Mitchelle Daka, and Tamunosoye Karibi-George. What a year it’s been for African beauty queens. From Nigeria to Tanzania and Uganda, women across the continent are making their mark in pageantry, winning international titles, taking on national crowns and preparing to represent their countries on some of the world’s biggest stages. And there’s so much to know about the women behind these crowns. We’re talking about a medical doctor championing women’s health, a laboratory scientist making history internationally, and advocates using their platforms to support causes they care about. So if you love keeping up with the continent’s brightest trailblazers, these five reigning beauty queens definitely need to be on your radar. Osele Iruomachukwu: Miss Continental World 2026 Osele officially made history by claiming the inaugural title of Miss Continental World 2026 in Ayutthaya, Thailand. When she isn’t serving pure editorial elegance on international runways, she is busy putting her medical laboratory science degree and entrepreneurial background to work. Bringing home a major global win, she is representing Nigeria with serious pride and showing the world what true excellence looks like on the world stage. Osele Iruomachukwu after winning the inaugural Miss Continental World 2026 title in Thailand. Photo Credit: Osele Iruomachukwu/Instagram Jihan Mohin Dimack: Miss Grand International 2026 Tanzania’s very own Jihan Mohin Dimack completely took the international pageantry scene by storm at the coronation in Bangkok, Thailand, making history as the first African woman to win the coveted Miss Grand International 2026 crown. Combining striking runway charm with a fierce passion for peace advocacy and global humanitarian work, Jihan has captured the hearts of audiences across multiple continents. Jihan Mohin Dimack celebrating her historic win as Miss Grand International 2026 in Bangkok, Thailand. Photo Credit: Jihan Mohin Dimack/Instagram Mitchelle Daka: Miss Universe Uganda 2026 Crowned Miss Universe Uganda 2026, Mitchelle Daka is carrying her country’s hopes straight to the global stage as she prepares to represent Uganda at the 75th Miss Universe competition in Puerto Rico. An international model and businesswoman, Mitchelle is all about breaking boundaries and using her platform to advocate for mental health awareness while encouraging young people to chase their dreams no matter what stands in their way. Mitchelle Daka representing Uganda as Miss Universe Uganda 2026. Photo Credit: Mitchelle Daka/Instagram Danielle Adewusi: Miss Universe Nigeria 2026 If her face looks familiar, it’s because Danielle Adewusi is not just a powerhouse beauty queen—she’s a qualified medical doctor who graduated from King’s College London. item.title: Cardi B Makes Her Tiny Desk Debut With “Bodak Yellow,” “Be Careful” & More | Watch
item.description: Autographed polaroid photo of Cardi B at the NPR Music office for her Tiny Desk Concert set. Photo Credit: NPR Music/Instagram If you thought you knew what a Cardi B live set looked like, think again. The rap superstar recently stepped into the NPR Music office for her debut Tiny Desk Concert, and the atmosphere was nothing short of electric. Word got out fast, drawing one of the biggest crowds the office has ever seen as people from all walks of life lined up to watch hip-hop’s most unfiltered star take over the iconic workspace. Dressed sharply in leather trousers and a power blazer, Cardi brought a refreshingly humble and humorous spirit to the desk, delivering a masterclass in stage presence. Kicking things off with the haunting synths and outright confidence of “ Hello ,” she immediately set the tone before riding that unstoppable energy into a reimagined version of “ ErrTime .” Never one to shy away from versatility, she then shifted gears into deeply personal material, performing the vulnerable “ Man of Your Word ” and “ Be Careful ” while keeping her trademark wit and humor intact. “Change the vibes, change the vibes,” she joked with a smile, before bringing the ultimate party back with “ Up ,” which slid straight into “ AH HA .” To close out the unforgettable set, she treated the packed room to two pivotal anthems from her legendary catalogue: “ Bodak Yellow ,” the breakout hit that started it all, and the boogaloo-heavy crowd-pleaser “ I Like It .” By the end of the set, Cardi was swinging her hips right along with the ecstatic crowd, leaving the room beaming with gratitude and handing out warm hugs to a few lucky audience members. It is safe to say the Desk has never seen anything quite like it.
